//! Referential actions on delete (LLP 3000.039 §3): before a delete removes
//! its row, reserve a schema-fixed charge, close over the `cascade`
//! references, refuse while a `restrict` reference still holds a closure row
//! from outside the closure, clear `set null` references outside it, and
//! remove the closure children first. The caller then removes the row itself.
// @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — closure first; probes exclude the closure; deletion dominates set null.
use crate::engine::runner::Runner;
use crate::{
    error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError},
    meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter},
    rows::{Bounds, Dir},
    schema::{Effect, references::{OnDelete, Referencing}},
    value::Value,
};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

impl Runner<'_> {
    pub(super) fn apply_reference_actions(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        if !schema.is_referenced(table_name) { return Ok(()); }
        let Some(price) = schema.delete_reservation(table_name) else {
            // A device without a reached child's exported price cannot charge
            // what the server charges; the server always has every price.
            if self.device { return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting {table_name} needs every referencing table's write price; queued without a local delete"))); }
            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{table_name}'s delete actions have no reservation: a cascading reference lacks its cap or its child's write price (guide writes)")));
        };
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#4.2 — what the commit publishes is fixed by the schema, not by the rows the actions reach.
        let closure = schema.action_tables(table_name);
        for table in &closure.written {
            if schema.visible(table) { self.written_tables.insert(table.clone()); }
            self.action_tables.insert(table.clone());
        }
        for table in &closure.read { self.read_tables.insert(table.clone()); }
        if !closure.written.is_empty() { self.tx.widen_change_evidence(); }
        for (kind, amount) in [(MeterKind::Steps, price[0]), (MeterKind::IndexEntries, price[1]), (MeterKind::Examined, price[2]), (MeterKind::RowsWritten, price[3]), (MeterKind::OutputBytes, price[5]), (MeterKind::RuleProbes, price[6])] {
            if amount > 0 { self.meter.charge(kind, amount)?; }
        }
        // Pending event images survive the closure and subsequent statements.
        // Keep their schema-fixed reservation until the request ends.
        let events = schema.delete_event_heap(table_name).unwrap_or(0);
        self.meter.heap(events)?;
        let mark = self.meter.mark();
        self.meter.heap(price[4].saturating_sub(events))?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — draw the reservation's rows from the request's physical allowance before the first seek.
        if !self.context.is_system() { self.tx.draw(table_name, price[2])?; }
        let meter = std::mem::replace(&mut self.meter, Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort));
        let prepaid = self.tx.reference_prepaid(true);
        let action = std::mem::replace(&mut self.engine_action, true);
        let result = self.reference_closure(table_name, old);
        self.engine_action = action;
        self.tx.reference_prepaid(prepaid);
        self.meter = meter;
        self.meter.release_heap(mark);
        result
    }

    /// Steps 3–6. The walk holds identities, never images: each child scan
    /// streams `PAGE` rows per seek, and every write rereads its row current.
    fn reference_closure(&mut self, root_table: &str, root: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        let mut seen: BTreeSet<(String, String)> = BTreeSet::from([(root_table.to_owned(), root.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned())]);
        // (Vectors, not maps: the web device pays for every new collection type.)
        let mut visits: Vec<(String, Value)> = vec![(root_table.to_owned(), root.field("id")?.clone())];
        // 3. Close over cascades, breadth first. Every reached row's referencing groups must be held on a device.
        let mut next = 0;
        while next < visits.len() {
            let (table, id) = visits[next].clone();
            next += 1;
            for r in schema.referencing(&table) {
                if self.device && !through_reference(&r) { self.prove_reference_held(&r, &id)?; }
                if r.action != OnDelete::Cascade { continue; }
                self.each_child(&r, &id, true, &mut |_, child| {
                    if seen.insert((r.child.to_owned(), child.as_str()?.to_owned())) { visits.push((r.child.to_owned(), child)); }
                    Ok(true)
                })?;
            }
        }
        // 4. Restrict: every probe runs, streaming past closure rows (the root
        // included) to the first outside witness; the first occupied reference
        // in schema order is reported. One reference's probes visit each closure
        // row at most once, plus one witness per probe (LLP 3000.039 §5.1).
        let mut occupied: Option<(String, String, String)> = None;
        for (table, id) in &visits {
            for r in schema.referencing(table) {
                if r.action != OnDelete::Restrict || through_reference(&r) { continue; }
                let mut outside = false;
                self.each_child(&r, id, false, &mut |_, child| {
                    outside = !seen.contains(&(r.child.to_owned(), child.as_str()?.to_owned()));
                    Ok(!outside)
                })?;
                let candidate = (r.child.to_owned(), r.column.to_owned(), table.clone());
                if outside && occupied.as_ref().is_none_or(|o| candidate < *o) { occupied = Some(candidate); }
            }
        }
        if let Some((child, column, parent)) = occupied {
            #[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
            self.refusing_clause(&child, &format!("{column}: {parent} (on delete restrict)"));
            let via = if parent == root_table { String::new() } else { format!(", through a {parent} row this delete cascades to") };
            return Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED", message: format!("{root_table} at {} is still referenced through {child}.{column} (on delete restrict){via}; delete or retarget those rows first, or declare the reference's action (guide writes)", self.statement_site) });
        }
        // A cascaded row can itself have a physically retained read-through
        // child. Decide that blocker before set-null writes begin, so expiry
        // can retain this root and continue without relying on transaction
        // rollback to undo a partial closure.
        for (table, id) in visits.iter().skip(1) {
            if self.physical_children_outside(table, id, &seen)? {
                return Err(self.parent_has_children(table));
            }
        }
        // 5. Set null outside the closure. Each group is gathered whole before
        // any of it is cleared: a clear can recount a sibling that shares the
        // reference's index and move it behind a page cursor. Each row is then
        // reread current before its write.
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#3 — gather, then clear: no row moves out of a walk it has not finished.
        for (table, id) in &visits {
            for r in schema.referencing(table) {
                if r.action != OnDelete::SetNull { continue; }
                let mut group: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
                self.each_child(&r, id, true, &mut |_, child| {
                    let child = child.as_str()?.to_owned();
                    if !seen.contains(&(r.child.to_owned(), child.clone())) { group.push(child); }
                    Ok(true)
                })?;
                for child in group {
                    let current = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, r.child, &child))?;
                    if let Some(current) = current.filter(|row| row.field(r.column).is_ok_and(|v| v == id)) {
                        self.clear_reference(r.child, r.column, current)?;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // 6. Delete the closure, children first, each from its current image.
        let reached: Vec<(String, String)> = visits[1..].iter().map(|(t, id)| Ok((t.clone(), id.as_str()?.to_owned()))).collect::<Result<_, RuntimeError>>()?;
        drop(visits);
        for (table, id) in deletion_order(schema, &reached) {
            let current = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.get(allowance, &table, &id))?;
            let Some(current) = current else { continue };
            self.delete_reached(&table, current)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Streams the ids of the live rows referencing `id` through `r` to
    /// `visit`, through its index, until `visit` answers false. A capped walk
    /// (cascade, set null) reads `PAGE` rows per seek and holds at most the
    /// reference's cap; a restrict probe reads one row per seek, so it examines
    /// nothing past its witness. Images are dropped before `visit` runs. Seeks
    /// start at the live suffix, so an expired backlog is never visited.
    fn each_child(&mut self, r: &Referencing<'_>, id: &Value, capped: bool, visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&mut Self, Value) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let schema = self.schema;
        let index = schema.reference_index(r.child, r.column).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} has no reference index", r.child, r.column)))?.to_owned();
        let (cap, page_rows) = if capped { (schema.reference_cap(r.child, r.column).map_or(u64::MAX, u64::from), PAGE) } else { (u64::MAX, 1) };
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#2.3 — seek on the effective deadline (a read-through child's `$deadline`), so no expired row is visited.
        let ranges = if r.table.expiry_column().is_some() && !through_reference(r) {
            let now = self.context.now.ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("delete clock is not pinned".into()))?;
            vec![(vec![id.clone(), Value::Null], None), (vec![id.clone()], Some(Value::Int(now)))]
        } else {
            vec![(vec![id.clone()], None)]
        };
        let mut live = 0_u64;
        for (prefix, gt) in ranges {

            loop {
                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, r.child, &index, &prefix, &bounds, Dir::Asc, page_rows))?;
                let more = page.len() == page_rows;
                if let Some((_, key)) = page.last() { bounds.after = crate::key::decode(key).map(|v| v.into_iter().skip(prefix.len()).collect()); }
                let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(page.len());
                for (row, _) in page {
                    if self.device {
                        // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — a device predicts only over current rows: retained history queues the delete, and only a live, current (or own provisional) row is a witness.
                        // A retained, no longer current row is work the reservation does not
                        // price and a witness the device cannot judge: the delete queues.
                        if self.tx.retained_row(r.child, &row)? && !self.tx.current_row(r.child, &row)? {
                            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting meets retained {} history that references it; queued without a local delete", r.child)));
                        }
                        if self.expired(r.table, &row) || !(self.tx.current_row(r.child, &row)? || self.is_provisional(r.child, &row)?) {
                            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting needs a current image of every {} row that references it; queued without a local delete", r.child)));
                        }
                    } else if self.expired(r.table, &row) { continue; }
                    live += 1;
                    // Activation validates caps and every write keeps them; more than the cap
                    // is a store that broke its own invariant, never a hidden-row count.
                    if live > cap { return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} holds more rows than its cap for one {} row", r.child, r.column, r.column))); }
                    ids.push(row.field("id")?.clone());
                }
                for child in ids {
                    if !visit(self, child)? { return Ok(()); }
                }
                if !more { break; }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// A device predicts only over a referencing group it holds completely.
    // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — the held-group proof of LLP 3000.007 §20.5, per closure row and reference.
    fn prove_reference_held(&mut self, r: &Referencing<'_>, id: &Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let index = self.schema.reference_index(r.child, r.column).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{}.{} has no reference index", r.child, r.column)))?.to_owned();
        let (child, key) = (r.child.to_owned(), [id.clone()]);
        // Key-decided readability, and the group itself held (a rejoined or
        // unacquired range is unknown even when the rule admits the viewer).
        if self.device_work(|runner| runner.upsert_absence_proven(&child, &index, &key))? && self.tx.current_group(&child, &index, &key)? { return Ok(()); }
        Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!("deleting needs every {} row that references it held; queued without a local delete", r.child)))
    }

    /// The engine's own write of a `set null` reference: no rule, every constraint.
    fn clear_reference(&mut self, table: &str, column: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        let mut new = old.clone();
        if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut new { fields.insert(column.to_owned(), Value::Null); }
        let patch = crate::value::object([(column, Value::Null)]);
        let outer = std::mem::replace(&mut self.engine_action, true);
        let result = self.target_attempt(table, |runner| {
            runner.reserve_maintains(table, &runner.schema.tables[table])?;
            runner.replace_authorized(table, old, new, true, &patch, 0)
        });
        self.engine_action = outer;
        result
    }

    /// The engine's own delete of a closure row: no rule, its constraints, its
    /// `read through` children's probe, maintains and partition events.
    fn delete_reached(&mut self, table_name: &str, old: Value) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
            runner.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Delete)?;
            let table = &runner.schema.tables[table_name];
            runner.reserve_maintains(table_name, table)?;
            runner.delete_row(table_name, old)
        })
    }
}

/// Rows a child scan holds per seek: the reservation's transient `4 × row`
/// (LLP 3000.039 §5.1, `Schema::delete_reservation`).
const PAGE: usize = crate::schema::references::REFERENCE_PAGE;

fn through_reference(r: &Referencing<'_>) -> bool {
    r.table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| t.reference == r.column)
}

/// The closure's rows, children before parents: a table goes first when no
/// other reached table must be removed before it (the cascade and `read
/// through` edges are acyclic by `check`), and within a table, later
/// discoveries first.
fn deletion_order(schema: &crate::schema::Schema, reached: &[(String, String)]) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    let tables: Vec<&str> = {
        let mut seen = Vec::new();
        for (table, _) in reached { if !seen.contains(&table.as_str()) { seen.push(table.as_str()); } }
        seen
    };
    // edges: child table -> the reached tables it must be removed before
    // (its cascade parents and its `read through` parent; LLP 3000.039 §3).
    let mut edges: Vec<(&str, &str)> = Vec::new();
    for &child in &tables {
        for &parent in &tables {
            if child != parent && schema.deletion_precedes(child, parent) { edges.push((child, parent)); }
        }
    }
    let mut order: Vec<&str> = Vec::new();
    let mut remaining = tables.clone();
    while !remaining.is_empty() {
        // A table no remaining table references can go now (its referencers are gone).
        let position = remaining.iter().position(|t| !remaining.iter().any(|other| other != t && edges.contains(&(*other, *t))))
            .unwrap_or(remaining.len() - 1);
        order.push(remaining.remove(position));
    }
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(reached.len());
    for table in order {
        out.extend(reached.iter().rev().filter(|(t, _)| t == table).cloned());
    }
    out
}

   161	                return if occupied { Err(runner.parent_has_children(parent)) } else { Ok(()) };
   162	            }
   163	            for name in &children {
   164	                let never = runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone(), Value::Null], &Bounds::default(), Dir::Asc, 1)?;
   165	                let finite = runner.tx.scan(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &Bounds { gt: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() }, Dir::Asc, 1)?;

   169	                // §3.3 forbids physical removal even when §6's live probe is empty.
   170	                // The author's implementation ruling keeps this case fail-closed.

   172	                    return Err(runner.parent_has_children(parent));
   173	                }
   174	            }

   176	        })

   178	
   179	    pub(super) fn parent_has_children(&self, parent: &str) -> RuntimeError {
   180	        RuntimeError::Structural {
   181	            code: "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN",
   182	            message: format!("{parent} at {} has stored children; delete its live read-through children and sweep expired children, then retry `delete {parent}[id]` (guide rules)", self.statement_site),
   183	        }
   184	    }
   185	
   186	    // @ref LLP 3000.014#5 — retained history cannot terminally refuse a
   187	    // current delete. Mismatched, expired or uncovered witnesses must queue.
   188	    fn current_children(&mut self, parent: &str, id: &Value, children: &[String]) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
   189	        if children.is_empty() { return Ok(false); }
   190	        let uncertain = || RuntimeError::Prediction("parent deletion needs complete matching current child coverage; queued without a row".into());
   191	        self.meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   192	        self.meter.heap(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[parent]))?;
   193	        // Device-only work over held state: the token counts it on the device's separate physical allowance.
   194	        let parent_id = id.as_str()?.to_owned();
   195	        let parent_row = self.authorized_scan(&[], |runner, scope| runner.tx.get(scope, parent, &parent_id))?.ok_or_else(uncertain)?;
   196	        for name in children {
   197	            let table = &self.schema.tables[name];
   198	            let through = table.through.as_ref().unwrap();
   199	            if !self.child_coverage(name, through, &parent_row)? { return Err(uncertain()); }
   200	            let table_scratch = self.meter.mark();
   201	            // Expected captures plus a reusable row/cursor, reserved before seeking.
   202	            self.meter.heap(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(table).saturating_mul(3))?;
   203	            let mut expected = crate::value::object([] as [(&str, Value); 0]);
   204	            stamp(&self.schema.tables[parent], through, &parent_row, &mut expected)?;
   205	            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
   206	            loop {
   207	                let scratch = self.meter.mark();
   208	                self.meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
   209	                self.meter.step(through.fields.len() as u64 + 1)?;
   210	                let page = self.authorized_scan(&[], |runner, scope| runner.tx.scan_metered(scope, name, CHILDREN, &[id.clone()], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 1, &mut runner.meter))?;
   211	                let Some((row, key)) = page.into_iter().next() else { break };
   212	                if self.engine_action && self.tx.retained_row(name, &row)? { return Err(uncertain()); }
   213	                if !self.tx.retained_row(name, &row)? {
   214	                    if self.expired(table, &row)
   215	                        || !(self.tx.current_row(name, &row)? || self.is_provisional(name, &row)?)
   216	                        || !capture_matches(through, &expected, &row) { return Err(uncertain()); }
   217	                    return Ok(true);
   218	                }
   219	                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key).map(|key| key.into_iter().skip(1).collect());

   221	            }
   222	            self.meter.release_heap(table_scratch);
   223	        }
   224	        Ok(false)
   225	    }
   226	}
   227	
   228	pub(super) fn capture_matches(through: &Through, expected: &Value, row: &Value) -> bool {
   229	    through.fields.keys().map(String::as_str).chain([PARENT_DEADLINE])
   230	        .all(|field| row.field(field).ok() == expected.field(field).ok())
   231	}
   232	
   233	pub(super) fn stamp(
   234	    parent: &Table,
   235	    through: &Through,
   236	    image: &Value,
   237	    row: &mut Value,
   238	) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   239	    let image = crate::schema::row_image(image, parent);
   240	    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = row {
   241	        for (capture, source) in &through.fields {
   242	            fields.insert(capture.clone(), image.field(source)?.clone());
   243	        }
   244	        fields.insert(
   245	            PARENT_DEADLINE.into(),
   246	            parent
   247	                .deadline(&image)
   248	                .map(Value::Int)
   249	                .unwrap_or(Value::Null),
   250	        );
   251	    }
   252	    Ok(())
   253	}

   435	impl super::runner::Runner<'_> {
   436	    /// Authoritative adapters feed an ancestor-ordered batch to the ordinary
   437	    /// insert/update path; captures always resolve inside this transaction.
   438	    pub fn seed_server_rows(
   439	        &mut self,
   440	        rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
   441	    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   442	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   443	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   444	                "server seed requires system authority".into(),
   445	            ));
   446	        }
   447	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   448	        let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
   449	        rows.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| order.iter().position(|x| x == n));
   450	        let count = rows.len() as u64;
   451	        for (name, row) in rows {
   452	            super::timeline::check_import(self.schema, &name)?;
   453	            // Adoption rewrites are system imports of stored images (LLP 3000.015 §1).
   454	            self.upsert(
   455	                &name,
   456	                &row.field("id")?.clone(),
   457	                row.import_input(&super::ImportInput(())),
   458	            )?;
   459	        }
   460	        self.check_final_exists()?;
   461	        Ok(count)
   462	    }
   463	
   464	    /// A bounded child-first sweep on the common Rows interface.
   465	    pub fn sweep_server_rows(&mut self, limit: usize, expiry_after: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   466	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   467	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   468	                "server sweep requires system authority".into(),
   469	            ));
   470	        }
   471	        let now = self
   472	            .context
   473	            .now
   474	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("sweep clock is not pinned".into()))?;
   475	        let mut count = 0;
   476	        let mut visited = 0;
   477	        let tables = resume_expiry_tables(self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev().collect(), expiry_after);
   478	        for name in tables {
   479	            let Some((index, _)) = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index() else {
   480	                continue;
   481	            };
   482	            let due = Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
   483	            let mut bounds = due.clone();
   484	            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(&name).cloned();
   485	            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
   486	            while visited < limit {
   487	                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
   488	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, scope| {
   489	                    runner
   490	                        .tx
   491	                        .scan(scope, &name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, batch)
   492	                })?;
   493	                if page.is_empty() {
   494	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   495	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   496	                        bounds = due.clone();
   497	                        wrapped = true;
   498	                        continue;
   499	                    }
   500	                    break;
   501	                }
   502	                let page_len = page.len();
   503	                for (row, key) in page {
   504	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   505	                    if let Some(after) = &bounds.after { expiry_after.insert(name.clone(), after.clone()); }
   506	                    visited += 1;
   507	                    mark_expiry_table(expiry_after, &name);
   508	                    match self.retire_expired_row(&name, &row) {
   509	                        Ok(true) => count += 1,
   510	                        Ok(false) => {},
   511	                        Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED" | "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", .. }) => {},
   512	                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
   513	                    }
   514	                }
   515	                if page_len < batch {
   516	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   517	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   518	                        bounds = due.clone();
   519	                        wrapped = true;
   520	                        continue;
   521	                    }
   522	                    break;
   523	                }
   524	            }
   525	        }
   526	        Ok(count)
   527	    }
   528	}

    11	) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
    12	    let current = tx.query(

    26	            tx,
    27	            schema,
    28	            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
    29	            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
    30	            tx.next_seq()?,
    31	        );

    53	fn references(kind: &ColumnType, value: &Value, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>) {

    66	fn rewrite_legacy_reference(
    67	    kind: &ColumnType,
    68	    value: &mut Value,
    69	    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
    70	) -> bool {
    71	    match (kind, value) {
    72	        (ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
    73	            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
    74	            *id = next.clone();
    75	            true
    76	        }
    77	        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_reference(inner, value, ids),
    78	        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
    79	            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
    80	        _ => false,
    81	    }
    82	}

    88	) -> bool {

    98	// @ref LLP 3000.007.003#3.0 — identity adoption covers every surviving typed reference, including dormant storage.
    99	pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(
   100	    tx: &Tx<'_>,
   101	    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
   102	) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   103	    if ids.values().all(BTreeMap::is_empty) || !enabled(tx)? { return Ok(0); }

   105	
   106	    let cells = tx.conn().prepare(
   107	        "SELECT v.t,v.id,v.column_name,v.data,c.definition FROM _dormant_values v JOIN _catalog k ON k.num=v.t JOIN _dormant_columns c ON c.table_name=k.name AND c.column_name=v.column_name ORDER BY v.t,v.id,v.column_name"
   108	    )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?, row.get::<_,String>(4)?)))?
   109	        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
   110	    for (t, id, column, data, definition) in cells {
   111	        let definition: Column = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
   112	        let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;

   114	            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_values SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3 AND column_name=?4", params![canonical_json(&value),t,id,column])?;
   115	            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
   116	        }
   117	    }
   118	
   119	    let rows = tx.conn().prepare(
   120	        "SELECT r.t,r.id,r.data,d.definition FROM _dormant_rows r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t JOIN _dormant_tables d ON d.table_name=c.name ORDER BY r.t,r.id"
   121	    )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?)))?
   122	        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
   123	    for (t, id, data, definition) in rows {
   124	        let table: Table = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
   125	        let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
   126	        if rewrite_legacy_row(&table, &mut row, ids) {
   127	            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_rows SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3", params![canonical_json(&row),t,id])?;
   128	            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
   129	        }
   130	    }
   131	
   132	    let narrowed = if super::narrowed::present(tx.conn())? {
   133	        tx.conn().prepare(
   134	            "SELECT t,id,data,definition FROM _dormant_narrow_rows ORDER BY t,id"
   135	        )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?)))?
   136	            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?
   137	    } else { Vec::new() };
   138	    for (t, id, data, definition) in narrowed {
   139	        let table: Table = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
   140	        let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
   141	        if rewrite_legacy_row(&table, &mut row, ids) {
   142	            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_narrow_rows SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3", params![canonical_json(&row),t,id])?;
   143	            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
   144	        }
   145	    }

   147	    for (target, target_ids) in ids {

   152	            tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _dormant_refs WHERE parent_t=?1 AND parent_id=?2", params![parent_t,old])?;
   153	        }

    54	impl Runner<'_> {
    55	    // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — no predicted delta enters receipt-derived state.
    56	    pub(super) fn defer_receipt_maintain(&self, m: &Maintain) -> bool {
    57	        self.device && self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target)
    58	    }
    59	
    60	    // Cache ordinary group keys once per target/query. Predicates and receipt
    61	    // fields are never evaluated; unknown/computed keys conservatively freeze
    62	    // the target. An unpinned read is incomplete if any group is dirty, while
    63	    // each returned row still decides independently whether to recount.
    64	    #[inline(never)]
    65	    pub(super) fn receipt_maintain_pending(&mut self, m: &Maintain, group: Option<&[Value]>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
    66	        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(false); }
    67	        if !self.receipt_pending_groups.contains_key(&m.target) {
    68	            let fields = if let Some(k) = &m.row_key { vec![k.source_key.clone()] }
    69	                else { m.by.iter().map(|f| m.aliases.get(f).unwrap_or(f).clone()).collect() };
    70	            let mut groups = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&m.source, &fields, !m.computed.is_empty())?;
    71	            if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
    72	                let member = self.receipt_overlay_groups(&k.table, std::slice::from_ref(&k.member_key), false)?;
    73	                groups = groups.zip(member).map(|(mut source, member)| { source.extend(member); source });
    74	            }
    75	            self.receipt_pending_groups.insert(m.target.clone(), groups);
    76	        }
    77	        let dirty = self.receipt_pending_groups[&m.target].as_ref().is_none_or(|keys|
    78	            group.map_or(!keys.is_empty(), |group| keys.iter().any(|key| key == group)));
    79	        if dirty {
    80	            self.value_source_incomplete = true;
    81	            self.components.note(|frame| frame.pending = true);
    82	        }
    83	        Ok(dirty)
    84	    }

    86	    fn receipt_overlay_groups(&self, table: &str, fields: &[String], computed: bool) -> Result<Option<Vec<Vec<Value>>>, RuntimeError> {
    87	        if !self.tx.has_provisional(table)? { return Ok(Some(Vec::new())); }
    88	        if computed || fields.iter().any(|f| self.schema.receipt_dependencies.get(table).is_some_and(|owned| owned.contains(f))) {
    89	            return Ok(None);
    90	        }
    91	        self.tx.provisional_groups(table, fields)
    92	    }

    94	    // Recover a read's parent/group from the pinned index. A member point uses
    95	    // one ordinary-key lookup; a scan without the parent stays conservative.
    96	    pub(super) fn receipt_read_group(&mut self, m: &Maintain, index: &str, key: &[Value]) -> Result<Option<Vec<Value>>, RuntimeError> {
    97	        if !self.defer_receipt_maintain(m) { return Ok(None); }
    98	        let columns = self.schema.tables[&m.target].indexes[index].columns();
    99	        let pinned = |field: &str| columns.iter().position(|c| c == field).and_then(|i| key.get(i)).cloned();
   100	        if let Some(k) = &m.row_key {
   101	            if let Some(parent) = pinned(&k.member_key) { return Ok(Some(vec![parent])); }
   102	            if let Some(id) = pinned("member").or_else(|| pinned("id")) {
   103	                let row = self.metered_scan(|r, scope| r.tx.get(scope, &k.table, id.as_str()?))?;
   104	                return Ok(row.and_then(|row| row.field(&k.member_key).ok().cloned()).map(|v| vec![v]));
   105	            }
   106	            return Ok(None);
   107	        }
   108	        Ok(m.by.iter().map(|f| pinned(f)).collect())

   111	    pub(super) fn maintain(&mut self, source: &str, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   112	        self.receipt_pending_groups.clear();
   113	        // Inserts ordinarily charge their actual aggregate work. A deferred
   114	        // predicate cannot select that work on a device, so use the same public
   115	        // worst-case reservation as update/delete before skipping it. Already
   116	        // prepaid writes must not pay twice.
   117	        if self.device && !self.maintain_prepaid && self.schema.maintains.iter().any(|m|
   118	            m.source == source && m.private.is_none() && m.row_key.is_none() && (self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&m.target) || self.schema.tables[&m.target].sync.is_none())) {
   119	            self.reserve_maintains(source, &self.schema.tables[source])?;
   120	        }
   121	        self.maintain_row_views(source, old, new)?;
   122	        let maintains = self.schema.maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.source == source && maintain.row_key.is_none());
   123	        for maintain in maintains {
   124	            if self.defer_receipt_maintain(maintain) || (self.device && self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].sync.is_none()) { continue; }
   125	            let source_bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.source]);
   126	            let target = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.target];
   127	            let bytes = source_bytes.saturating_mul(2).saturating_add(super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(target).saturating_mul(16 + 4 * target.indexes.len() as u64));
   128	            let prepaid = self.maintain_prepaid;
   129	            if maintain.private.is_some() && self.column_prepaid { self.maintain_prepaid = true; }
   130	            let result = self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| runner.maintain_one(maintain, old, new));
   131	            self.maintain_prepaid = prepaid;
   132	            result?;
   133	        }
   134	        Ok(())
   135	    }

   137	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.9 — reserve interpreted images, both keys, targets and index buffers before allocation; release transient ownership on every exit.
   138	    pub(super) fn maintain_scratch<T>(&mut self, bytes: u64, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   139	        if self.maintain_prepaid { return work(self); }
   140	        self.meter.heap(bytes)?;
   141	        let result = work(self);
   142	        self.meter.used.heap_bytes = self.meter.used.heap_bytes.saturating_sub(bytes);
   143	        result
   144	    }

   146	    fn maintain_one(&mut self, maintain: &Maintain, old: Option<&Value>, new: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   147	        let table = self.schema.table(&maintain.source).expect("validated");
   148	        let mut changes: Vec<(Vec<Value>, i128)> = Vec::new();
   149	        for (image, direction) in [(old, -1), (new, 1)] {
   150	            let Some(image) = image else { continue };

    53	fn references(kind: &ColumnType, value: &Value, out: &mut Vec<(String, String)>) {

    55	        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => references(inner, value, out),
    56	        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) => {
    57	            for value in values {

    74	            *id = next.clone();

    77	        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_reference(inner, value, ids),
    78	        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>

   111	fn int_range(kind: &ColumnType) -> bool {
   112	    match kind {
   113	        ColumnType::IntRange { .. } => true,
   114	        ColumnType::Optional(inner) | ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => int_range(inner),
   115	        _ => false,
   116	    }
   117	}
   118	
   119	fn ordered_units(table: &Table, rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   120	    let units = |term: &RuleTerm| matches!(term, RuleTerm::Field(f) if matches!(table.columns.get(f), Some(ColumnType::Decimal { .. } | ColumnType::Money { .. })));
   121	    match rule {
   122	        RuleExpr::Compare(_, l, r) => units(l) || units(r),
   123	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|item| ordered_units(table, item)),
   124	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered_units(table, inner),
   125	        _ => false,
   126	    }
   127	}
   128	
   129	fn ordered(rule: &RuleExpr) -> bool {
   130	    match rule {
   131	        RuleExpr::Compare(..) => true,
   132	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(ordered),
   133	        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => ordered(inner),
   134	        _ => false,
   135	    }
   136	}

    60	        client: Client,
    61	        name: &str,
    62	        mut schema: Schema,
    63	        programs: impl IntoIterator<Item = Program>,
    64	    ) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
    65	        let name = namespace(name)?;
    66	        refuse_maintained_columns(&schema)?;
    67	        super::columns::validate_before_prepare(&schema)?;
    68	        schema.prepare_contribution_indexes();
    69	        let programs: BTreeMap<_, _> = programs.into_iter().map(|p| (p.name.clone(), p)).collect();
    70	        supported(&schema, &programs)?;
    71	        Self::attach(client, schema, programs, Some(&name))
    72	    }
    73	
    74	    /// Reopen the persisted compiled generation; subsequent transactions refuse
    75	    /// if another connection activates a successor.
    76	    pub fn open(mut client: Client, name: &str) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
    77	        let name = namespace(name)?;
    78	        client.batch_execute(&format!("SET search_path = {name}, pg_catalog;"))?;
    79	        let row = client.query_one("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?;
    80	        if row.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
    81	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
    82	        }
    83	        let schema = decode(row.get(1))?;
    84	        let programs = decode(row.get(2))?;
    85	        supported(&schema, &programs)?;
    86	        // Existing immutable stores adopt this portable admission policy at open.
    87	        // Return one offending index and its exact count, never its row payloads.
    88	        if let Some(row) = client.query(
    89	            "SELECT t, ix, COUNT(*) FROM i WHERE octet_length(k) > $1 GROUP BY t, ix ORDER BY t, ix LIMIT 1",
    90	            &[&(crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as i32)],
    91	        )?.first() {
    92	            return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(row.get(0), row.get(1), row.get::<_, i64>(2) as u64));
    93	        }
    94	        Self::attach(client, schema, programs, None)
    95	    }
    96	
    97	    // @ref LLP 3000.033#1.3 — read-session storage and all other upgrades
    98	    // commit together, only after every open/adoption check has succeeded.
    99	    fn attach(client: Client, mut schema: Schema, programs: BTreeMap<String, Program>, create: Option<&str>) -> Result<Self, RuntimeError> {
   100	        let mut store = Store::new(client);
   101	        let tx = store.opening_transaction()?;
   102	        tx.batch("SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s'; SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s';")?;
   103	        if let Some(name) = create {
   104	            tx.batch(&format!("CREATE SCHEMA {name}; SET search_path = {name}, pg_catalog;"))?;
   105	            tx.batch(store::DDL)?;
   106	            tx.execute("INSERT INTO _backend VALUES (true,$1,$2,$3)",
   107	                &[&store::VERSION, &canonical_json(&schema), &canonical_json(&programs)])?;
   108	        }
   109	        tx.query("SELECT seq FROM _head WHERE singleton FOR UPDATE", &[])?;
   110	        // Admission must use the backend that survived the wait for the head.
   111	        // A format change can leave schema/program bytes unchanged.
   112	        let held = tx.query("SELECT version,schema,programs FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?.remove(0);
   113	        if held.get::<_, &str>(0) != store::VERSION {
   114	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));
   115	        }
   116	        let held_schema: Schema = decode(held.get(1))?;
   117	        let held_programs: BTreeMap<String, Program> = decode(held.get(2))?;
   118	        supported(&held_schema, &held_programs)?;
   119	        if held_schema.hash() != schema.hash() || canonical_json(&held_programs) != canonical_json(&programs) {
   120	            return Err(RuntimeError::Generation("the backend changed while opening; reopen its current generation".into()));
   121	        }
   122	        // Even a no-op ALTER takes an exclusive table lock. Reopening an
   123	        // upgraded store must remain possible while another reader holds it.
   124	        for (column, ddl) in [
   125	            ("generation", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN generation BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1"),
   126	            ("through_shortened", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN through_shortened TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'"),
   127	            ("maintained_identity_version", "ALTER TABLE _backend ADD COLUMN maintained_identity_version TEXT"),
   128	        ] {
   129	            let exists: bool = tx.query("SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = '_backend'::regclass AND attname = $1 AND NOT attisdropped)", &[&column])?[0].get(0);
   130	            if !exists { tx.batch(ddl)?; }
   131	        }
   132	        // Repeat admission under the head fence used by physical adoption.
   133	        if let Some(row) = tx.query(
   134	            "SELECT t, ix, COUNT(*) FROM i WHERE octet_length(k) > $1 GROUP BY t, ix ORDER BY t, ix LIMIT 1",
   135	            &[&(crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as i32)],
   136	        )?.first() {
   137	            return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(row.get(0), row.get(1), row.get::<_, i64>(2) as u64));
   138	        }
   139	        tx.batch("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _sequences (parent TEXT NOT NULL, id TEXT NOT NULL, value BIGINT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(parent, id));")?;
   140	        tx.batch(store::READ_SESSIONS_DDL)?;
   141	        tx.batch("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS _log_row_seq; DROP INDEX IF EXISTS _log_row_seq_kind;")?;
   142	        caps::install(&tx, &schema)?;
   143	        let generation = contribution_upgrade::install(&tx, &mut schema)?;
   144	        let generation = maintained_identity_upgrade::install(&tx, &schema, create.is_some(), generation)?;
   145	        // Retain the adapter's ordinary connection limits on successful open.
   146	        tx.batch("SET statement_timeout = '5s'; SET lock_timeout = '5s';")?;
   147	        tx.commit()?;
   148	        store.generation = generation;
   149	        schema.prepare_delivery_lookup();
   150	        Ok(Self { store, schema, programs, ceilings: Ceilings::default(), mode: WriteMode::Serialized, retries: 0, precharge: Metered::default(), expiry_after: BTreeMap::new() })
   151	    }

   179	    pub fn query(&mut self, name: &str, context: Context) -> Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal> {
   180	        self.query_with_delivery(name, context, super::DeliveryManifest::Build)
   181	    }
   182	
   183	    pub fn query_with_delivery(&mut self, name: &str, mut context: Context, manifest: super::DeliveryManifest) -> Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal> {
   184	        context.generation = self.generation();
   185	        let program = self.programs.get(name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::UnknownOp(name.into()))?;
   186	        if program.kind != ProgramKind::Query {
   187	            return Err(RuntimeError::UnknownOp(format!("{name} is not a query")).into());
   188	        }
   189	        super::server_query_allowed(&self.schema, name)?;
   190	        validate::validate_inputs(&self.schema, program, &mut context.args)?;
   191	        context.now.get_or_insert_with(crate::now_ms);
   192	        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
   193	        let seq = tx.next_seq()? - 1;
   194	        let mut runner = Runner::new(&tx, &self.schema, context, Meter::new(self.ceilings, Cut::Cap), seq);
   195	        runner.meter.used = self.precharge;
   196	        let data = runner.run(program)?;
   197	        runner.charge_output(&data)?;
   198	        let (delivery, delivery_meter) = match manifest { super::DeliveryManifest::Build => runner.delivery_manifest(&data), super::DeliveryManifest::Skip => (None, None) };
   199	        let outcome = QueryOutcome { decoration_expiry: runner.decoration_expiry, search_rows: runner.search_rows.take(), search_scopes: None, delivery, delivery_meter, ephemeral: None,
   200	            unavailable: runner.query_unavailable,
   201	            complete: runner.meter.capped_at.is_none()
   202	                && runner.word_cut_at.is_none()
   203	                && !runner.non_uniform
   204	                && !runner.page_overflow
   205	                && !runner.value_source_incomplete
   206	                && !runner.page_position_lost(),
   207	            cut: runner.read_cut(),
   208	            capped_at: runner.meter.capped_at.clone(),
   209	            word_cut_at: runner.word_cut_at.clone(),
   210	            next: runner.outcome_next_cursor()?,
   211	            data,
   212	            seq,
   213	            metered: runner.meter.used,
   214	            tables: runner.read_tables.iter().cloned().collect(),
   215	            next_expiry: runner.next_expiry.get(),
   216	        };
   217	        drop(runner);
   218	        tx.rollback()?;
   219	        Ok(outcome)
   220	    }

   222	    pub fn replay(&mut self, viewer: &str, op: &str) -> Result<Option<MutationOutcome>, RuntimeError> {
   223	        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
   224	        let receipt = tx.applied(viewer, op)?;
   225	        tx.rollback()?;
   226	        receipt.as_deref().map(MutationOutcome::from_receipt).transpose()

   231	    fn replay_mutation(&mut self, viewer: &str, id: &str, name: &str, args_digest: &str) -> Result<Option<MutationOutcome>, RuntimeError> {
   232	        let tx = self.store.transaction(None)?;
   233	        let receipt = tx.applied_bound(viewer, id, name, args_digest)?;
   234	        tx.rollback()?;
   235	        receipt.as_deref().map(MutationOutcome::from_receipt).transpose()
   236	    }

   238	    pub fn mutate(&mut self, name: &str, op: Option<&str>, mut context: Context) -> Result<MutationOutcome, RuntimeError> {
   239	        context.generation = self.generation();

   244	        // unknown or renamed programs. Never return a historical result row.

   256	            context.entropy = crate::ids::seed();

   269	        unreachable!()
   270	    }

   272	    fn mutate_once(&mut self, program: &Program, op: Option<&str>, mut context: Context, args_digest: &str) -> Result<MutationOutcome, RuntimeError> {

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs

@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+//! Atomic adoption of the maintained-row address function in the evaluation
+//! adapter. The marker and generation publish in the same writer transaction
+//! as the target rebuild, so no writer can observe mixed legacy/digest ids.
+use super::*;
+
+pub(super) fn install(
+    tx: &store::Tx<'_>,
+    schema: &Schema,
+    creating: bool,
+    generation: u64,
+) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+    let current = tx.query(
+        "SELECT maintained_identity_version FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
+        &[],
+    )?[0].get::<_, Option<&str>>(0).map(str::to_owned);
+    if current.as_deref() == Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION) {
+        return Ok(generation);
+    }
+
+    let aggregates: Vec<_> = schema.maintains.iter()
+        .filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none())
+        .cloned()
+        .collect();
+    if !creating && !aggregates.is_empty() {
+        let mut runner = Runner::new(
+            tx,
+            schema,
+            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
+            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
+            tx.next_seq()?,
+        );
+        runner.event_free = true;
+        for maintain in &aggregates {
+            runner.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
+        }
+    }
+
+    let generation = if creating || aggregates.is_empty() {
+        generation
+    } else {
+        generation.checked_add(1)
+            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?
+    };
+    tx.execute(
+        "UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=$1, generation=$2 WHERE singleton",
+        &[&crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION, &store::signed(generation)?],
+    )?;
+    Ok(generation)
+}

+fn reopening_legacy_maintained_ids_rebuilds_before_publishing_the_generation() {

+    let mut engine = PostgresEngine::create(Client::connect(&url, postgres::NoTls).unwrap(), &name, schema, programs).unwrap();
+    engine.load([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(7))]))]).unwrap();
+    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let target = engine.schema.tables["totals"].clone();
+    let generation = engine.generation();
+    let tx = engine.store.transaction(Some(WriteMode::Serialized)).unwrap();
+    let old = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().expect("current aggregate");
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &old).unwrap();
+    let mut old = old;
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut old {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &old, None).unwrap();
+    tx.execute("UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=NULL WHERE singleton", &[]).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    drop(engine);
+
+    let mut reopened = PostgresEngine::open(Client::connect(&url, postgres::NoTls).unwrap(), &name).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(reopened.generation(), generation + 1);
+    let tx = reopened.store.transaction(None).unwrap();
+    assert!(tx.get("totals", &legacy).unwrap().is_none());
+    let rebuilt = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().expect("digest aggregate");
+    assert_eq!(rebuilt.field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

+fn has_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match kind {
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table } => ids.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| !ids.is_empty()),
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner)
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. }
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => has_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, ids),
+        _ => false,
+    }

+fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    value: &mut Value,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
+            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
+            *id = next.clone();
+            true
+        }
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, value, ids),
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
+        _ => false,
+    }

+#[test]
+fn seeded_source_retirement_precedes_final_exists_and_rolls_back() {
+    let source = r#"
+table conversations:
+  public
+table members:
+  conversationId: conversations
+  seen: int
+  cap 10 by conversationId
+  public
+table messages:
+  conversationId: conversations
+  ordinal: int
+  until: time ?
+  expire at .until
+  public
+table witnesses:
+  message: messages on delete cascade
+  unique byMessage: message
+  cap 1 by message
+  public
+table gates:
+  message: messages
+  public
+  after insert <- exists witnesses[message = .message] by byMessage
+table fixtures:
+  until: time ?
+  expire at .until
+  public
+view unread: count messages by members m
+  where .conversationId = m.conversationId and .ordinal > m.seen
+"#;
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("seed-final-exists.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let schema: Schema = crate::json_codec::from_text(
+        &crate::json_codec::to_text(&bound.schema).unwrap(),
+    ).unwrap();
+    let message = |until| object([
+        ("id", id("m")), ("conversationId", id("c")),
+        ("ordinal", Value::Int(1)), ("until", Value::Int(until)),
+    ]);
+    let witness = object([("id", id("w")), ("message", id("m"))]);
+    let gate = object([("id", id("g")), ("message", id("m"))]);
+
+    let mut e = Engine::memory(schema.clone(), vec![]).unwrap();
+    let refused = e.seed_at([
+        ("messages".into(), message(5)),
+        ("witnesses".into(), witness.clone()),
+        ("gates".into(), gate.clone()),
+    ], 10);
+    assert!(matches!(refused, Err(crate::RuntimeError::Constraint(_))), "{refused:?}");
+    for table in ["messages", "witnesses", "gates", "unread"] {
+        assert!(e.store().rows(table).unwrap().is_empty(), "{table} survived refused seed");
+    }
+
+    // A live source leaves the witness intact, while an unrelated expired
+    // fixture retains the ordinary physical seed contract.
+    let mut e = Engine::memory(schema, vec![]).unwrap();
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("messages".into(), message(50)),
+        ("witnesses".into(), witness),
+        ("gates".into(), gate),
+        ("fixtures".into(), object([("id", id("f")), ("until", Value::Int(5))])),
+    ], 10).unwrap();
+    for table in ["messages", "witnesses", "gates", "fixtures"] {
+        assert_eq!(e.store().rows(table).unwrap().len(), 1, "{table}");
+    }
+}

+fn legacy_identity_adoption_can_change_the_grouping_key() {
+    let mut e = groups();
+    let schema = e.schema().clone();
+    let target = schema.tables["totals"].clone();
+    let rows = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    for old in rows {
+        tx.delete("totals", &target, &old).unwrap();
+        let mut legacy = old.clone();
+        let id = crate::value::canonical_json(&[old.field("n").unwrap().clone()]);
+        if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut legacy {
+            fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(id));
+        }
+        tx.put("totals", &target, &legacy, None).unwrap();
+    }
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute(
+        "DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1",
+        [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META],
+    ).unwrap();
+
+    let next = compile(&GROUPS.replace("by .n", "by .bucket"));
+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 10).unwrap();
+    let rows = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(rows.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(rows[0].field("id").unwrap(),
+        &Value::Id(crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(0)])));
+    assert_eq!(rows[0].field("bucket").unwrap(), &Value::Int(0));
+    assert_eq!(rows[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(4));

 use super::*;

+fn rewrite_legacy_reference(
+    kind: &ColumnType,
+    value: &mut Value,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
+            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
+            *id = next.clone();
+            true
+        }
+        (ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_reference(inner, value, ids),
+        (ColumnType::List { of, .. } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+
+fn rewrite_legacy_row(
+    table: &Table,
+    row: &mut Value,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    let (Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields)) = row else { return false };
+    table.columns.iter().fold(false, |changed, (column, kind)| {
+        fields.get_mut(column).is_some_and(|value| rewrite_legacy_reference(kind, value, ids)) || changed
+    })
+}
+
+/// Rewrite references retained outside the active namespace alongside their
+/// active counterparts. References whose aggregate target was itself retired
+/// have no map and retain the ordinary dormant-lifetime refusal on restore.
+// @ref LLP 3000.007.003#3.0 — identity adoption covers every surviving typed reference, including dormant storage.
+pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(
+    tx: &Tx<'_>,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+    if ids.values().all(BTreeMap::is_empty) || !enabled(tx)? { return Ok(0); }
+    let mut rewritten = 0_u64;
+
+    let cells = tx.conn().prepare(
+        "SELECT v.t,v.id,v.column_name,v.data,c.definition FROM _dormant_values v JOIN _catalog k ON k.num=v.t JOIN _dormant_columns c ON c.table_name=k.name AND c.column_name=v.column_name ORDER BY v.t,v.id,v.column_name"
+    )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?, row.get::<_,String>(4)?)))?
+        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
+    for (t, id, column, data, definition) in cells {
+        let definition: Column = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        if rewrite_legacy_reference(&definition.kind, &mut value, ids) {
+            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_values SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3 AND column_name=?4", params![canonical_json(&value),t,id,column])?;
+            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
+        }
+    }
+
+    let rows = tx.conn().prepare(
+        "SELECT r.t,r.id,r.data,d.definition FROM _dormant_rows r JOIN _catalog c ON c.num=r.t JOIN _dormant_tables d ON d.table_name=c.name ORDER BY r.t,r.id"
+    )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?)))?
+        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
+    for (t, id, data, definition) in rows {
+        let table: Table = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        if rewrite_legacy_row(&table, &mut row, ids) {
+            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_rows SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3", params![canonical_json(&row),t,id])?;
+            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
+        }
+    }
+
+    let narrowed = if super::narrowed::present(tx.conn())? {
+        tx.conn().prepare(
+            "SELECT t,id,data,definition FROM _dormant_narrow_rows ORDER BY t,id"
+        )?.query_map([], |row| Ok((row.get::<_,i64>(0)?, row.get::<_,String>(1)?, row.get::<_,String>(2)?, row.get::<_,String>(3)?)))?
+            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?
+    } else { Vec::new() };
+    for (t, id, data, definition) in narrowed {
+        let table: Table = serde_json::from_str(&definition).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        let mut row: Value = serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e|RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
+        if rewrite_legacy_row(&table, &mut row, ids) {
+            tx.conn().execute("UPDATE _dormant_narrow_rows SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id=?3", params![canonical_json(&row),t,id])?;
+            rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
+        }
+    }
+
+    for (target, target_ids) in ids {
+        if target_ids.is_empty() { continue; }
+        let parent_t = tx.num(target)?;
+        for (old, next) in target_ids {
+            tx.conn().execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO _dormant_refs(t,id,column_name,parent_t,parent_id,invalid) SELECT t,id,column_name,parent_t,?1,invalid FROM _dormant_refs WHERE parent_t=?2 AND parent_id=?3", params![next,parent_t,old])?;
+            tx.conn().execute("DELETE FROM _dormant_refs WHERE parent_t=?1 AND parent_id=?2", params![parent_t,old])?;
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(rewritten)
+}

+#[test]
+fn legacy_aggregate_identity_migrates_dormant_references_before_restore() {
+    const BASE: &str = "table entries:\n  n: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .n\n  public\n";
+    const WITH_SAVED: &str = "table entries:\n  n: int\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .n\n  public\ntable saved:\n  target: totals\n  public\n";
+    let mut e = engine(WITH_SAVED);
+    seed(&mut e, "entries", serde_json::json!({"id":"e","n":7}));
+    let digest = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap()[0].field("id").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_owned();
+    seed(&mut e, "saved", serde_json::json!({"id":"s","target":digest}));
+
+    // Model a release-store row written by 0.4.28, before digest identities.
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let target = e.schema().tables["totals"].clone();
+    let saved = e.schema().tables["saved"].clone();
+    let old_target = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap().remove(0);
+    let old_saved = e.store().rows("saved").unwrap().remove(0);
+    let mut legacy_target = old_target.clone();
+    let mut legacy_saved = old_saved.clone();
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut legacy_target { fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone())); }
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut legacy_saved { fields.insert("target".into(), Value::Id(legacy)); }
+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.delete("saved", &saved, &old_saved).unwrap();
+    tx.put("saved", &saved, &legacy_saved, None).unwrap();
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &old_target).unwrap();
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &legacy_target, None).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    e.store().conn().execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1", [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META]).unwrap();
+
+    // Removing `saved` retains it outside the active namespace while the
+    // aggregate target remains active. Identity adoption must rewrite both
+    // the hidden row and its dormant-reference ledger before setting marker.
+    activate(&mut e, BASE, 2).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().meta(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META).unwrap().as_deref(), Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION));
+    activate(&mut e, WITH_SAVED, 3).unwrap();
+    let restored = e.store().rows("saved").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(restored.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(restored[0].field("target").unwrap(), &Value::Id(digest));
+}

+  expiry retirement, the engine records each seeded final-exists obligation
+  that does hold. Every such witness must still exist after retirement and its

+  and Postgres use this same pre/post invariant. A `test` case may `expect`

+    fn final_exists_holds(&mut self, table_name: &str, row: &Value, constraint: &Constraint) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
+        let Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { table: target, index, key } = constraint else { return Ok(true);
+        };
+        let table = self.schema.table(table_name).expect("validated").clone();
+        let has_references = key.iter().any(|term| term.reference_source().is_some());

+            // row supplying its key before it can confer authority.
+            let rule = crate::schema::RuleExpr::Exists { table: target.clone(), index: index.clone(), key: key.clone(), equalities: vec![], provenance: crate::ir::KeyProvenance::Shape };
+            for term in key { if let crate::schema::RuleTerm::Field(field) = term { self.provisional_sequence_read |= self.device && table.sequences.contains_key(field); } }

+            };
+            key

+            .iter()
+            .map(|term| match term {
+                crate::schema::RuleTerm::Field(field) | crate::schema::RuleTerm::NextField(field) => {
+                    // This inserted image owns a provisional ordinal even if no expression read it.

+                }

+                crate::schema::RuleTerm::Literal(value) => value.clone(),
+                crate::schema::RuleTerm::OldField(_) | crate::schema::RuleTerm::Reference { .. } | crate::schema::RuleTerm::ReferenceChain { .. } => Value::Null,

     1	import Quarry.Eval
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Writes: rule checks and refusals
     5	
     6	From the rules card, `why E_RULE`, `why NOT_FOUND`, `why E_CONFLICT` and the
     7	writes card:
     8	
     9	* **insert** — the insert rule judges the new image (`E_RULE`); a clash on
    10	  `id` or a declared unique key with a hidden row is `E_RULE`; with a visible
    11	  row, `if absent` returns null and an ordinary insert refuses `E_CONSTRAINT`
    12	  or the key's `else CODE`.
    13	* **update** — "readable" means the read rule admits the old row before the
    14	  write; the update rule judges old and next. Denial is `E_RULE` on a readable
    15	  target and `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable one; a missing target is
    16	  `NOT_FOUND`; an `if` condition on an unreadable target is `NOT_FOUND`, and a
    17	  false one on a readable target `E_CONFLICT`; a secondary unique clash is
    18	  `NOT_FOUND` (unreadable target), `E_RULE` (hidden colliding row) or
    19	  `E_CONSTRAINT`. An admitted update may change a hidden row; the result is
    20	  the row if it is readable afterwards, else null.
    21	* **upsert** — patches an existing target as an update; inserts an absent
    22	  one, where an incomplete image or insert-rule denial is `NOT_FOUND`.
    23	* **delete** — `NOT_FOUND` for a missing or unreadable refused target,
    24	  `E_RULE` for a readable one whose delete rule refuses. A row that
    25	  `restrict`, `cascade` or `set null` references name also needs read
    26	  authority (`NOT_FOUND`); then its delete closes over `cascade` references,
    27	  refuses `E_REFERENCED` while a `restrict` reference names a closure row
    28	  from outside the closure, clears `set null` references outside it, and
    29	  removes the closure (LLP 3000.039 §3).
    30	
    31	The order in which checks run when several fail is not documented; the
    32	model's order is OPEN W1–W6.
    33	-/
    34	
    35	namespace Quarry
    36	
    37	def notFound : Stop := .refuse "NOT_FOUND"
    38	def eRule : Stop := .refuse "E_RULE"
    39	def eInput : Stop := .refuse "E_INPUT"
    40	
    41	def toScalarE : Value → Except Stop Scalar
    42	  | .s x => pure x
    43	  | _ => throw eInput

    45	def scalarsE (fs : List (String × Value)) : Except Stop (List (String × Scalar)) :=
    46	  fs.mapM fun p => do return (p.1, ← toScalarE p.2)

    48	/-- A column value fits its declaration: only a nullable column takes null. -/
    49	def fits (c : ColDecl) (x : Scalar) : Bool := c.nullable || x != .null
    50	
    51	/-- The new image of an insert. An absent nullable column is null; an absent
    52	required column refuses with `missing`. Unknown fields refuse `E_INPUT`. -/
    53	def buildImage (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) (fields : List (String × Scalar))
    54	    (missing : Stop) : Except Stop Row := do
    55	  if fields.any fun p => p.1 != "id" && !(td.cols.any (·.name == p.1)) then throw eInput
    56	  let cols ← td.cols.mapM fun c => match fields.lookup c.name with
    57	    | some x => if fits c x then pure (c.name, x) else throw eInput
    58	    | none => if c.nullable then pure (c.name, Scalar.null) else throw missing
    59	  return { id := rid, cols }
    60	
    61	/-- The next image of an update: the patch replaces named columns. -/
    62	def patchImage (td : TableDecl) (old : Row) (patch : List (String × Scalar)) : Except Stop Row := do
    63	  if patch.any fun p => !(td.cols.any (·.name == p.1)) then throw eInput
    64	  let cols ← old.cols.mapM fun p => match patch.lookup p.1 with
    65	    | some x =>
    66	      match td.cols.find? (·.name == p.1) with
    67	      | some c => if fits c x then pure (p.1, x) else throw eInput
    68	      | none => throw eInput
    69	    | none => pure p
    70	  return { old with cols }
    71	
    72	def keyOf (cols : List String) (r : Row) : List (String × Scalar) := cols.map fun c => (c, r.get c)
    73	
    74	/-- The first unique key (in order) on which another row (not `except`)
    75	collides with `img`. Keys with a null component never collide (a nullable
    76	unique key permits tied nulls; indexes card). -/
    77	def findClash (rows : List Row) (keys : List (List String)) (img : Row) (except : Option (List Nat)) :
    78	    Option (Nat × Row) :=
    79	  let rec go (i : Nat) : List (List String) → Option (Nat × Row)
    80	    | [] => none
    81	    | k :: ks =>
    82	      let kv := keyOf k img
    83	      if kv.any (·.2 == .null) then go (i + 1) ks
    84	      else match rows.find? (fun r => keyMatch kv r && except != some r.id) with
    85	        | some r => some (i, r)
    86	        | none => go (i + 1) ks
    87	  go 0 keys

    89	/-- The refusal for a visible clash on unique key `i` of `["id"] ++ uniques`
    90	(`withId`) or of `uniques`. -/
    91	def clashCode (td : TableDecl) (withId : Bool) (i : Nat) : Stop :=
    92	  let j := if withId then i - 1 else i
    93	  if withId && i = 0 then .refuse "E_CONSTRAINT"
    94	  else match td.uniqueCodes[j]? with
    95	    | some (some code) => .refuse code
    96	    | _ => .refuse "E_UNIQUE"

    99	  if ks.any (·.2 == .null) then none else rows.find? (keyMatch ks)

   111	  if readable sch s v t r then r.toValue else .null

   114	    (t : String) (r : Row) : Value :=

   118	def guardE (b : Bool) (e : Stop) : Except Stop Unit := if b then .ok () else .error e

   120	def doInsertImage (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
   121	    (img : Row) (clashHidden : Stop) :
   122	    Except Stop (Value × Store) := do
   123	  -- Insert authority has already been checked. Remaining unique checks and
   124	  -- the physical insertion use the post-retirement store.
   125	  match findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td now)) (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none with
   126	  | some (i, r) => do
   127	    guardE (readableAt sch s v now t r) clashHidden

   129	  | none =>

   131	    pure (resultOfAt sch s' v now t img, s')

   133	/-- An update's `if` condition: `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable target,
   134	`E_CONFLICT` when false. -/
   135	def condCheck (rd : Bool) (cond : Option (Row → Except Stop Bool)) (old : Row) : Except Stop Unit :=
   136	  match cond with
   137	  | some f => do
   138	    guardE rd notFound
   139	    let b ← f old
   140	    guardE b (.refuse "E_CONFLICT")
   141	  | none => pure ()
   142	
   143	/-- A secondary unique clash of an update's next image with another row. -/
   144	def clashCheck (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) (t : String) (td : TableDecl)
   145	    (rd : Bool) (old nw : Row) : Except Stop Unit :=
   146	  match findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td now)) td.uniques nw (some old.id) with
   147	  | some (i, r) =>
   148	    throw (if !rd then notFound else if !(readableAt sch s v now t r) then eRule else clashCode td false i)
   149	  | none => pure ()

   152	    (old : Row) (patch : List (String × Scalar)) (cond : Option (Row → Except Stop Bool)) :
   153	    Except Stop (Value × Store) := do

   174	/-! ## Referential actions (LLP 3000.039 §3) -/
   175	
   176	/-- Every reference that names table `t` and carries an action:
   177	`(child table, column, action)`. -/
   178	def referencing (sch : Schema) (t : String) : List (String × String × OnDelete) :=
   179	  sch.tables.flatMap fun td => td.cols.filterMap fun c =>
   180	    match c.ref, c.onDelete with
   181	    | some p, some a => if p == t then some (td.name, c.name, a) else none
   182	    | _, _ => none
   183	
   184	/-- Row `k` names the row with id `i` through column `c`. -/
   185	def names (k : Row) (c : String) (i : List Nat) : Bool := k.get c == .id i
   186	
   187	def inClosure (cl : List (String × Row)) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   188	  cl.any fun p => p.1 == t && p.2.id == r.id
   189	
   190	/-- The rows one step of cascades reaches from `(t, r)`. -/
   191	def cascadeKids (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : List (String × Row) :=
   192	  (referencing sch t).flatMap fun (c, col, a) =>
   193	    if a == .cascade then ((s c).filter fun k => names k col r.id).map fun k => (c, k) else []
   194	
   195	/-- Breadth-first closure over `cascade` references, each row once; `fuel`
   196	bounds the walk (the store's row count suffices). -/
   197	def closure (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row)
   198	  | 0, _, acc => acc
   199	  | _ + 1, [], acc => acc
   200	  | f + 1, (t, r) :: rest, acc =>
   201	    let new := (cascadeKids sch s t r).foldl (fun n p => if inClosure (acc ++ n) p.1 p.2 then n else n ++ [p]) []
   202	    closure sch s f (rest ++ new) (acc ++ new)
   203	
   204	/-- Some `restrict` reference names a closure row from outside the closure. -/
   205	def restricted (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (cl : List (String × Row)) : Bool :=
   206	  cl.any fun (t, r) => (referencing sch t).any fun (c, col, a) =>
   207	    a == .restrict && (s c).any fun k => names k col r.id && !inClosure cl c k
   208	
   209	def clearCol (r : Row) (c : String) : Row :=
   210	  { r with cols := r.cols.map fun p => if p.1 == c then (p.1, Scalar.null) else p }
   211	
   212	/-- Clear every `set null` reference that names a closure row from outside it. -/
   213	def setNulls (sch : Schema) (cl : List (String × Row)) (s : Store) : Store :=
   214	  cl.foldl (fun s (t, r) => (referencing sch t).foldl (fun s (c, col, a) =>
   215	    if a == .setNull then
   216	      ((s c).filter fun k => names k col r.id && !inClosure cl c k).foldl
   217	        (fun s k => s.replaceRow c k (clearCol k col)) s
   218	    else s) s) s
   219	
   220	def storeSize (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat := sch.tables.foldl (fun n td => n + (s td.name).length) 0
   221	
   222	/-- The store after deleting `old` from `t` with its referential actions, or
   223	`E_REFERENCED`. With no action-carrying reference into `t`, exactly
   224	`removeRow` (LLP 3000.039 §1). -/
   225	def refDelete (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=
   226	  let cl := closure sch s (storeSize sch s + 1) [(t, old)] [(t, old)]
   227	  if restricted sch s cl then throw (.refuse "E_REFERENCED")
   228	  else pure (cl.foldl (fun s p => s.removeRow p.1 p.2) (setNulls sch cl s))
   229	
   230	/-- Apply actions to the physical store using only the rows that are logically
   231	live as action witnesses. The root may itself be absent from `witnesses`. -/
   232	def refDeleteFrom (sch : Schema) (witnesses physical : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=
   233	  let cl := closure sch witnesses (storeSize sch witnesses + 1) [(t, old)] [(t, old)]
   234	  if restricted sch witnesses cl then throw (.refuse "E_REFERENCED")
   235	  else
   236	    let physical := cl.foldl (fun s (parent, row) => (referencing sch parent).foldl (fun s (child, col, action) =>
   237	      if action == .setNull then
   238	        ((witnesses child).filter fun k => names k col row.id && !inClosure cl child k).foldl
   239	          (fun s witness => match (s child).find? fun current => current.id == witness.id with
   240	            | some current =>
   241	              if names current col row.id then s.replaceRow child current (clearCol current col) else s
   242	            | none => s) s
   243	      else s) s) physical
   244	    pure (cl.foldl (fun s p => s.removeRow p.1 p.2) physical)

   261	def retireExpiredSameId (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) (t : String)
