     3	/-!
     4	# Write authority
     5	
     6	**No write succeeds unless the corresponding rule holds.** A successful write
     7	either leaves the store unchanged (`insert … if absent` on a visible clash)
     8	or is one authorized `Step`: an insert whose insert rule admits the new
     9	image, an update whose update rule admits (old, next) for a row that exists,
    10	or a delete whose delete rule admits the row. Rules are evaluated in the
    11	opened projection of the store as it stood immediately before that write
    12	(`applyWrite_authorized`).
    13	
    14	A whole mutation's store transition is a chain of such steps
    15	(`mutation_authorized`).
    16	-/
    17	
    18	namespace Quarry
    19	
    20	inductive Step (sch : Schema) (v : List Nat) (now : Int) : Store → Store → Prop
    21	  | insert {s : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {r : Row} :
    22	      sch.table? t = some td → td.insert.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some r } = true →
    23	      Step sch v now s (s.insertRow t r)
    24	  | update {s : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old nw : Row} :
    25	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t →
    26	      td.update.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { old := some old, next := some nw } = true →
    27	      Step sch v now s (s.replaceRow t old nw)
    28	  /-- A delete whose delete rule admits the row, with the referential
    29	  actions the schema declares on the rows naming it (LLP 3000.039 §4.1: the
    30	  parent's delete authorizes a declared cascade or set null). -/
    31	  | delete {s s' : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old : Row} :
    32	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t →
    33	      td.delete.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some old } = true →
    34	      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok s' →
    35	      Step sch v now s s'
    36	  /-- An expired same-id row is retired inside an insert transaction before
    37	  the replacement image's remaining constraints are checked. -/
    38	  | retire {s s' : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old : Row} :
    39	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t → expired td now old = true →
    40	      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok s' →
    41	      Step sch v now s s'
    42	  /-- A same-id replacement is one authorized transition: its insert rule is
    43	  checked against the pre-retirement store, then the expired predecessor's
    44	  actions run, then the new image is inserted. -/
    45	  | replaceExpired {s retired : Store} {t : String} {td : TableDecl} {old img : Row} :
    46	      sch.table? t = some td → old ∈ s t → expired td now old = true →
    47	      td.insert.eval (openedStore sch s now) v { self := some img } = true →
    48	      refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old = .ok retired →
    49	      Step sch v now s (retired.insertRow t img)

   236	theorem sbind_ok {α β : Type} {x : EM α} {f : α → EM β} {rs : RS} {r : β × RS}

   242	theorem liftE_ok {α : Type} {x : Except Stop α} {rs : RS} {a : α} {rs' : RS}
   243	    (h : (liftE x).run rs = .ok (a, rs')) : x = .ok a := by
   244	  unfold liftE at h

   246	  | error e => cases h

   249	/-- Statement execution changes the world only through `Hooks.apply`: any
   250	relation on worlds that is reflexive, transitive and contains every applied
   251	write contains the whole execution. -/
   252	theorem execStmts_inv {W : Type} (H : Hooks W) (cx : Ctx) (R : W → W → Prop) (hrefl : ∀ w, R w w)
   253	    (htrans : ∀ a b d, R a b → R b d → R a d)
   254	    (happ : ∀ w rw val w', H.apply cx w rw = .ok (val, w') → R w w') :
   255	    ∀ fuel w env ss rs fl w' env' rs',
   256	      (execStmts H fuel cx w env ss).run rs = .ok ((fl, w', env'), rs') → R w w' := by
   257	  intro fuel
   258	  induction fuel with
   259	  | zero =>
   260	    intro w env ss rs fl w' env' rs' h
   261	    simp [execStmts, refuse, StateT.run, throw, throwThe, MonadExceptOf.throw, StateT.lift] at h
   262	    cases h
   263	  | succ fuel ih =>
   264	    intro w env ss rs fl w' env' rs' h
   265	    cases ss with
   266	    | nil =>
   267	      simp only [execStmts, StateT.run, pure, StateT.pure, Except.pure] at h
   268	      cases h; exact hrefl w
   269	    | cons s ss =>
   270	      cases s with
   271	      | assign x e =>
   272	        simp only [execStmts] at h
   273	        obtain ⟨p, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   274	        exact ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h
   275	      | require c code =>
   276	        simp only [execStmts] at h
   277	        obtain ⟨⟨v, _⟩, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   278	        obtain ⟨b, rs2, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   279	        split at h
   280	        · exact ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h
   281	        · simp [refuse, StateT.run, throw, throwThe, MonadExceptOf.throw, StateT.lift] at h; cases h
   282	      | ret e =>
   283	        simp only [execStmts] at h
   284	        obtain ⟨⟨v, nx⟩, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   285	        simp only [StateT.run, pure, StateT.pure, Except.pure] at h
   286	        cases h; exact hrefl w
   287	      | ite c th el =>
   288	        simp only [execStmts] at h
   289	        obtain ⟨⟨v, _⟩, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   290	        obtain ⟨b, rs2, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   291	        obtain ⟨⟨fl1, w1, env1⟩, rs3, h1, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   292	        have r1 := ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h1
   293	        split at h
   294	        · simp only [StateT.run, pure, StateT.pure, Except.pure] at h
   295	          cases h; exact r1
   296	        · exact htrans _ _ _ r1 (ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h)
   297	      | write bind op =>
   298	        simp only [execStmts] at h
   299	        obtain ⟨rs0, rs1, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   300	        obtain ⟨rw, rs2, -, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   301	        obtain ⟨⟨val, w1⟩, rs3, h1, h⟩ := sbind_ok h
   302	        exact htrans _ _ _ (happ _ _ _ _ (liftE_ok h1)) (ih _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h)

   304	theorem mutationHooks_apply_authorized {cx : Ctx} {w w' : MutationWorld}
   305	    {rw : RWrite} {val : Value}
   306	    (h : mutationHooks.apply cx w rw = .ok (val, w')) :
   307	    Steps cx.schema cx.viewer cx.now w.store w'.store := by
   308	  change (match applyWrite cx w.store rw with
   309	    | Except.error e => Except.error e
   310	    | Except.ok (value, store) =>
   311	      let changed := w.changed ++ changedFinalRows cx.schema w.store store
   312	      let changed := match rw.changedExplicitId? cx w.store with
   313	        | some address => changed ++ [address]
   314	        | none => changed
   315	      Except.ok (value, { store, changed := changed.eraseDups })) = Except.ok (val, w') at h
   316	  split at h
   317	  · cases h
   318	  · rename_i result store happ
   319	    cases h
   320	    exact applyWrite_authorized happ

     6	The executable engine uses SHA-256 over a domain-separated canonical group

The migration derives target-specific maps from predecessor identities, resolves aggregate-reference chains to a fixed point, and rewrites active and dormant references before rebuilding targets. PostgreSQL places this under its writer fence; I’m assessing that path statically. Next I’m comparing the formal model and differential driver with runtime ordering and lookup behavior.

     1	//! The engine against the Lean model (LLP 3000.035 §5.2).
     2	//!
     3	//! **The model side.** Each case's surface program goes through
     4	//! `snapback4_lang::emit::lean` (the parsed tree, never the binder's IR) to
     5	//! the model's case JSON, and through `quarry-oracle` (`snapback4/lean`,
     6	//! `lake build`), one long-lived process per worker that answers one tagged
     7	//! outcome per line. A case the emitter cannot translate is `Unsupported`
     8	//! under the emitter's named reason, never a pass.
     9	//!
    10	//! **The engine side.** The engine over SQLite (the ordinary in-memory
    11	//! server store) at `Ceilings::default()`, the ceilings a production server
    12	//! runs, not the case's stored budget; the model runs unbounded (its meter is
    13	//! abstract, OPEN M1).
    14	//!
    15	//! **Compared fields** (README, "How the harness compares"):
    16	//!
    17	//! - `kind`: answer, unavailable, refused, committed;
    18	//! - `code`: the refusal code (sites are not modelled);
    19	//! - `data` / `result`: exact, both sides as tagged values, so an id never
    20	//!   compares equal to a text (OPEN V1); rows compare as field maps;
    21	//! - `complete`: exact;
    22	//! - `next`: presence only (OPEN C1). When both carry one, each side
    23	//!   continues from its own cursor and the next page is compared
    24	//!   (`continuation-*`), until both are exhausted;
    25	//! - a mutation then runs `observe` on each side's resulting store
    26	//!   (`post-*`): the engine's store, and the model's committed store (or the
    27	//!   original store after a refusal).
    28	//!
    29	//! Meter fields, cut sites, `tables` and `seq` are not compared. Expiry
    30	//! sweeps advance both stores before the following program is compared.
    31	//!
    32	//! **Signatures** are `lean--{field}--{engine}~{model}`, each side's stable
    33	//! class (a refusal code, `unavailable`, `committed`, or the data's shape).
    34	//! The finding's `left` is the engine's raw record, `right` the model's raw
    35	//! outcome; the canonical forms compared are its `continuation`.
    36	// @ref LLP 3000.035#52-stage-2-a-small-lean-core — the Lean model as a further oracle over the Stage 1 generator.

    38	    ast::Body,
    39	    campaign::Report,
    40	    execute::{self, Outcome},
    41	    generate::Case,
    42	    oracle::{Finding, Oracle, Verdict},

    45	use snapback4_core::Ceilings;
    46	use snapback4_lang::emit::lean::LeanModule;
    47	use std::{
    48	    cell::RefCell,
    49	    collections::BTreeSet,
    50	    fs::{self, OpenOptions},
    51	    io::{BufRead, BufReader, Write},
    52	    path::PathBuf,
    53	    process::{Child, ChildStdin, ChildStdout, Command, Stdio},
    54	};
    55	
    56	/// The `quarry-oracle` executable: `SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE`, else the Lake
    57	/// build in this checkout.
    58	pub fn oracle_path() -> PathBuf {
    59	    match std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE") {
    60	        Some(p) => PathBuf::from(p),
    61	        None => PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../lean/.lake/build/bin/quarry-oracle"),
    62	    }
    63	}

    65	/// Bring this checkout's `quarry-oracle` up to date with its model sources
    66	/// (`lake build quarry-oracle`, under a second when current). A merge or
    67	/// checkout that changes `lean/` leaves the previous executable in `.lake`,
    68	/// and the harness would report that older model's choices as disagreements
    69	/// (2026-10-12: a stale pre-guard oracle on the merged `sb4-loop` tree showed
    70	/// `lean--complete--complete~incomplete`). Nothing is done when
    71	/// `SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE` names the oracle (the caller vouches for it; a
    72	/// campaign's workers inherit the refreshed path that way) or when `lake` is
    73	/// not installed (a missing oracle still refuses at `LeanProcess::spawn`).
    74	pub fn refresh() -> Result<(), String> {
    75	    if std::env::var_os("SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE").is_some() {
    76	        return Ok(());
    77	    }
    78	    let dir = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../lean");
    79	    // Keep the optional-tool path read-only, including a checkout whose model
    80	    // directory is not writable. A version probe writes no Lake build artifacts.
    81	    match Command::new("lake").arg("--version").current_dir(&dir).stdin(Stdio::null()).output() {
    82	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
    83	            eprintln!("lake not found: using the Lean oracle as built at {}", oracle_path().display());
    84	            return Ok(());
    85	        }
    86	        Err(e) => return Err(format!("lake: {e}")),
    87	        Ok(_) => {} // The build below reports actual toolchain/configuration errors.
    88	    }
    89	    // @ref LLP 3000.035#52-stage-2-a-small-lean-core — concurrent refreshes must not write the same Lake artifacts.
    90	    let cache = dir.join(".lake");
    91	    fs::create_dir_all(&cache).map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh cache: {e}"))?;
    92	    let refresh_lock = OpenOptions::new().create(true).truncate(false).read(true).write(true)
    93	        .open(cache.join("snapback4-refresh.lock")).map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh lock: {e}"))?;
    94	    refresh_lock.lock().map_err(|e| format!("Lean refresh lock: {e}"))?;
    95	    match Command::new("lake").args(["build", "quarry-oracle"]).current_dir(&dir).stdin(Stdio::null()).output() {
    96	        Ok(output) if output.status.success() => Ok(()),
    97	        Ok(output) => Err(format!(
    98	            "`lake build quarry-oracle` failed in {}: {}{}",
    99	            dir.display(),
   100	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
   101	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
   102	        )),
   103	        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
   104	            eprintln!("lake not found: using the Lean oracle as built at {}", oracle_path().display());
   105	            Ok(())
   106	        }
   107	        Err(e) => Err(format!("lake: {e}")),
   108	    }
   109	}

   111	/// One `quarry-oracle` process: a JSON case per line in, an outcome per line out.
   112	pub struct LeanProcess {
   113	    child: Child,
   114	    stdin: ChildStdin,
   115	    stdout: BufReader<ChildStdout>,
   116	}
   117	impl LeanProcess {
   118	    pub fn spawn() -> Result<Self, String> {
   119	        let path = oracle_path();
   120	        if !path.is_file() {
   121	            return Err(format!(
   122	                "Lean oracle missing: {} (run `cd snapback4/lean && lake build`, or set SNAPBACK4_LEAN_ORACLE)",
   123	                path.display()
   124	            ));
   125	        }
   126	        let mut child = Command::new(&path)
   127	            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
   128	            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
   129	            .stderr(Stdio::inherit())
   130	            .spawn()
   131	            .map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
   132	        let stdin = child.stdin.take().unwrap();
   133	        let stdout = BufReader::new(child.stdout.take().unwrap());
   134	        Ok(Self { child, stdin, stdout })
   135	    }
   136	    pub fn ask(&mut self, case: &Json) -> Result<Json, String> {
   137	        writeln!(self.stdin, "{case}").map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle write: {e}"))?;
   138	        self.stdin.flush().map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle flush: {e}"))?;
   139	        let mut line = String::new();
   140	        let n = self.stdout.read_line(&mut line).map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle read: {e}"))?;
   141	        if n == 0 {
   142	            return Err("Lean oracle exited".into());
   143	        }
   144	        let answer: Json = serde_json::from_str(&line).map_err(|e| format!("Lean oracle answer {line:?}: {e}"))?;
   145	        if answer["kind"] == "error" {
   146	            // A case the model cannot decode is an emitter defect, never a verdict.
   147	            return Err(format!("Lean oracle refused the case: {}", answer["error"]));
   148	        }
   149	        Ok(answer)
   150	    }
   151	}
   152	impl Drop for LeanProcess {
   153	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   154	        let _ = self.child.kill();
   155	        let _ = self.child.wait();
   156	    }
   157	}
   158	
   159	thread_local! {
   160	    static PROCESS: RefCell<Option<LeanProcess>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
   161	}
   162	
   163	/// Ask this thread's oracle process, starting it on first use and once
   164	/// more if it has died.
   165	pub fn ask(case: &Json) -> Result<Json, String> {
   166	    PROCESS.with(|cell| {
   167	        let mut slot = cell.borrow_mut();
   168	        if slot.is_none() {
   169	            *slot = Some(LeanProcess::spawn()?);
   170	        }
   171	        match slot.as_mut().unwrap().ask(case) {
   172	            Err(e) if e == "Lean oracle exited" => {
   173	                *slot = Some(LeanProcess::spawn()?);
   174	                slot.as_mut().unwrap().ask(case)
   175	            }
   176	            other => other,
   177	        }
   178	    })
   179	}

   181	/// The engine's value as the model's tagged value; rows as field maps.
   182	pub fn engine_value(v: &snapback4_core::Value) -> Json {
   183	    use snapback4_core::Value as V;
   184	    match v {
   185	        V::Null => json!({"null": null}),
   186	        V::Bool(b) => json!({"bool": b}),
   187	        V::Int(n) => json!({"int": n.to_string()}),
   188	        V::String(s) => json!({"text": s}),
   189	        V::Id(s) => json!({"id": s}),
   190	        V::Bytes(b) => json!({"bytes": b.iter().map(|x| format!("{x:02x}")).collect::<String>()}),
   191	        V::Row(fs) | V::Map(fs) => json!({"row": fs.iter().map(|(k, x)| (k.clone(), engine_value(x))).collect::<Map<_, _>>()}),
   192	        V::Array(xs) => json!({"arr": xs.iter().map(engine_value).collect::<Vec<_>>()}),
   193	    }
   194	}
   195	
   196	/// The model's tagged value with rows as field maps (its rows are ordered pairs).
   197	pub fn model_value(v: &Json) -> Json {
   198	    if let Some(xs) = v.get("arr").and_then(Json::as_array) {
   199	        return json!({"arr": xs.iter().map(model_value).collect::<Vec<_>>()});
   200	    }
   201	    if let Some(fs) = v.get("row").and_then(Json::as_array) {
   202	        let mut m = Map::new();
   203	        for p in fs {
   204	            m.insert(p[0].as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_owned(), model_value(&p[1]));
   205	        }
   206	        return json!({"row": m});
   207	    }
   208	    v.clone()
   209	}
   210	
   211	fn shape(v: &Json) -> String {
   212	    v.as_object().and_then(|o| o.keys().next().cloned()).unwrap_or_else(|| "value".into())
   213	}
   214	
   215	/// One side's comparable record: `kind`, then `code` or `data`/`complete`/`next`.
   216	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
   217	pub struct Canon {
   218	    pub kind: String,
   219	    pub code: Option<String>,
   220	    pub data: Option<Json>,
   221	    pub complete: Option<bool>,
   222	    pub next: bool,
   223	}
   224	impl Canon {
   225	    /// The side's stable class for a differing `field`: the field's own
   226	    /// value where it is a flag, else a code, kind or data shape.
   227	    pub fn class(&self, field: &str) -> String {
   228	        if field.ends_with("complete") {
   229	            return if self.complete == Some(true) { "complete" } else { "incomplete" }.into();
   230	        }
   231	        if field.ends_with("next") {
   232	            return if self.next { "next" } else { "no-next" }.into();
   233	        }
   234	        match (&self.code, &self.data) {
   235	            (Some(code), _) => code.clone(),
   236	            (None, Some(d)) if self.kind == "answer" => shape(d),
   237	            _ => self.kind.clone(),
   238	        }
   239	    }
   240	    fn json(&self) -> Json {
   241	        json!({"kind": self.kind, "code": self.code, "data": self.data, "complete": self.complete, "next": self.next})
   242	    }
   243	}
   244	
   245	pub fn engine_canon(o: &Outcome) -> Canon {
   246	    let blank = Canon { kind: String::new(), code: None, data: None, complete: None, next: false };
   247	    if let Some(r) = o.refusal() {
   248	        return Canon { kind: "refused".into(), code: r["code"].as_str().map(str::to_owned), ..blank };
   249	    }
   250	    if o.kind == "mutation" {
   251	        let result = serde_json::from_value::<snapback4_core::Value>(o.value["result"].clone()).map(|v| engine_value(&v)).unwrap_or(Json::Null);
   252	        return Canon { kind: "committed".into(), data: Some(result), ..blank };
   253	    }
   254	    if o.value.get("unavailable") == Some(&json!(true)) {
   255	        return Canon { kind: "unavailable".into(), ..blank };
   256	    }
   257	    let data = serde_json::from_value::<snapback4_core::Value>(o.value["data"].clone()).map(|v| engine_value(&v)).unwrap_or(Json::Null);
   258	    Canon { kind: "answer".into(), data: Some(data), complete: o.value["complete"].as_bool(), next: o.next().is_some(), ..blank }
   259	}
   260	
   261	pub fn model_canon(m: &Json) -> Canon {
   262	    let blank = Canon { kind: m["kind"].as_str().unwrap_or("error").to_owned(), code: None, data: None, complete: None, next: false };
   263	    match blank.kind.as_str() {
   264	        "refused" => Canon { code: m["code"].as_str().map(str::to_owned), ..blank },
   265	        "committed" => Canon { data: Some(model_value(&m["result"])), ..blank },
   266	        "answer" => Canon {
   267	            data: Some(model_value(&m["data"])),
   268	            complete: m["complete"].as_bool(),
   269	            next: m["next"] != json!({"null": null}),
   270	            ..blank
   271	        },
   272	        _ => blank,
   273	    }
   274	}
   275	
   276	/// The first differing field, in the order a reader wants it.
   277	pub fn differ(e: &Canon, m: &Canon) -> Option<&'static str> {
   278	    if e.kind != m.kind {
   279	        return Some("kind");
   280	    }
   281	    if e.code != m.code {
   282	        return Some("code");
   283	    }
   284	    if e.data != m.data {
   285	        return Some(if e.kind == "committed" { "result" } else { "data" });
   286	    }
   287	    if e.complete != m.complete {
   288	        return Some("complete");
   289	    }
   290	    if e.next != m.next {
   291	        return Some("next");
   292	    }
   293	    None
   294	}
   295	
   296	/// `lean--{field}--{engine class}~{model class}`.
   297	pub fn signature(field: &str, e: &Canon, m: &Canon) -> String {
   298	    format!("lean--{}--{}~{}", field.replace('_', "-"), e.class(field), m.class(field))
   299	}
   300	
   301	fn finding(field: &str, e: &Canon, m: &Canon, engine: Outcome, model: &Json, trail: Vec<Outcome>) -> Verdict {
   302	    Verdict::Disagree(Finding {
   303	        signature: signature(field, e, m),
   304	        oracle: Oracle::Lean,
   305	        field: field.into(),
   306	        left: engine,
   307	        right: Outcome { kind: "lean".into(), value: model.clone() },
   308	        continuation: trail,
   309	        store_trace: None,
   310	    })
   311	}
   312	
   313	fn trail_entry(e: &Canon, m: &Canon) -> Outcome {
   314	    Outcome { kind: "canonical".into(), value: json!({"engine": e.json(), "model": m.json()}) }
   315	}

   317	/// What one case comes to; `executed` counts engine and model calls.
   318	pub struct Checked {
   319	    pub verdict: Verdict,
   320	    pub executed: u64,
   321	    pub pages: u64,
   322	    pub mutation: bool,
   323	    /// The first outcome's class on an agreeing case (`committed`, a code,
   324	    /// `unavailable`, or the data's shape).
   325	    pub class: String,
   326	}

   328	/// The module, or why the case is outside the fragment.
   329	pub fn module(source: &str) -> Result<LeanModule, String> {
   330	    match snapback4_lang::emit::lean::lean(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]) {
   331	        Ok(module) => Ok(module),
   332	        Err(snapback4_lang::emit::lean::LeanError::Diagnostics(_)) => Err("parse".into()),
   333	        Err(snapback4_lang::emit::lean::LeanError::Unsupported(u)) => Err(u.reason),
   334	    }
   335	}
   336	
   337	/// Compare one case whose source compiles. `Err` is a harness or emitter
   338	/// defect (never a verdict).
   339	pub fn compare(case: &Case, source: &str) -> Result<Checked, String> {
   340	    let unsupported = |reason: String| Ok(Checked { verdict: Verdict::Unsupported(reason), executed: 0, pages: 0, mutation: false, class: String::new() });
   341	    let module = match module(source) {
   342	        Ok(m) => m,
   343	        Err(reason) => return unsupported(reason),
   344	    };
   345	    let mutation = case.program.mutation();
   346	    if let Err(u) = module.program("run") {
   347	        return unsupported(u.reason);
   348	    }
   349	    if mutation {
   350	        if let Err(u) = module.program("observe") {
   351	            return unsupported(format!("observe-{}", u.reason));
   352	        }
   353	    }
   354	    let store = match module.store(&case.rows) {
   355	        Ok(s) => s,
   356	        Err(u) => return unsupported(u.reason),
   357	    };
   358	    let mut m_args = match module.tag_args("run", &case.args) {
   359	        Ok(a) => a,
   360	        Err(u) => return unsupported(u.reason),
   361	    };
   362	    // The prelude: each step on the engine and on the model's store, in order.
   363	    for i in 0..case.steps.len() {
   364	        if let Err(u) = module.program(&format!("prep{i}")) {
   365	            return unsupported(format!("prelude-{}", u.reason));
   366	        }
   367	        if let Err(u) = module.tag_args(&format!("prep{i}"), &case.steps[i].args) {
   368	            return unsupported(format!("prelude-{}", u.reason));
   369	        }
   370	    }
   371	    let (mut engine, prelude) = execute::world(case, source)?;
   372	    engine.set_ceilings(Ceilings::default());
   373	    let mut executed = 0;
   374	    let mut pages = 0;
   375	    let mut store = store;
   376	    let mut sweep_cursor: Option<Json> = None;
   377	    let mut steps = prelude.iter();
   378	    let mut trail = vec![];
   379	    for (i, step) in case.steps.iter().enumerate() {
   380	        let name = format!("prep{i}");
   381	        if step.sweep {
   382	            let e_sweep = steps.next().ok_or("prelude sweep outcome missing")?;
   383	            if e_sweep.kind != "sweep" || e_sweep.value.get("error").is_some() {
   384	                return Err(format!("engine prelude sweep failed: {:?}", e_sweep.value));
   385	            }
   386	            let args = module.tag_args(&name, &step.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   387	            let viewer = step.viewer.as_deref().unwrap_or(&case.principal);
   388	            let mut sweep_case = module.case_at_sweep(&name, store.clone(), viewer, args, None, step.at, true).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   389	            sweep_case["sweepLimit"] = json!(10_000);
   390	            if let Some(cursor) = &sweep_cursor { sweep_case["sweepCursor"] = cursor.clone(); }
   391	            let swept = ask(&sweep_case)?;
   392	            executed += 1;
   393	            if swept["kind"] != "committed" { return Err(format!("Lean prelude sweep failed: {swept}")); }
   394	            store = swept["store"].clone();
   395	            sweep_cursor = Some(swept["result"].clone());
   396	        }
   397	        let e_raw = steps.next().ok_or("prelude outcome missing")?.clone();
   398	        let args = module.tag_args(&name, &step.args).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?;
   399	        let viewer = step.viewer.as_deref().unwrap_or(&case.principal);
   400	        let m_raw = ask(&module.case_at(&name, store.clone(), viewer, args, None, step.at).map_err(|u| u.to_string())?)?;
   401	        executed += 2;
   402	        let (e, m) = (engine_canon(&e_raw), model_canon(&m_raw));
   403	        trail.push(trail_entry(&e, &m));
   404	        if let Some(f) = differ(&e, &m) {
   405	            return Ok(Checked { verdict: finding(&format!("prelude-{f}"), &e, &m, e_raw, &m_raw, trail), executed, pages, mutation, class: String::new() });
   406	        }
   407	        if m.kind == "committed" {
   408	            store = m_raw["store"].clone();
   409	        }
   410	    }

     1	//! The Lean model's case format (LLP 3000.035 §5.2): a checked Quarry
     2	//! program, translated from its **surface** syntax tree into the terms of
     3	//! `snapback4/lean/Quarry/Syntax.lean`, as the JSON that
     4	//! `snapback4/lean/Quarry/CaseJson.lean` decodes (format:
     5	//! `snapback4/lean/README.md`, "The case format").
     6	//!
     7	//! **Why the surface tree.** The model is a second implementation of the
     8	//! binder and the interpreter together. Reading the binder's IR would copy
     9	//! the binder's decisions into the model's input, and the comparison could
    10	//! no longer find a binder defect. The input is the parsed [`Document`]s.
    11	//! Besides the fact that [`crate::compile`] reported no diagnostics, the case
    12	//! carries the checked schema's selected plain expiry-index columns: that
    13	//! physical choice determines observable cross-root action order and the
    14	//! across-call continuation tuple. The emitter independently selects the first
    15	//! eligible catalog entry; this qualifies execution given the planned index
    16	//! catalog, not the planner's index synthesis. No program IR is read.
    17	//!
    18	//! **Types.** The few places that need a type (a text literal beside an id is
    19	//! an id, OPEN V1; a positional key chooses a unique key by its argument
    20	//! types, indexes card) take it from the surface's own declarations, which
    21	//! the type checker has accepted: column types, argument types, helper
    22	//! parameters, `viewer : principal`, and literal kinds, propagated through
    23	//! locals by the small inference in [`Scope::ty`]. When that inference cannot
    24	//! decide, the program is unsupported, never guessed.
    25	//!
    26	//! **The expansions** are those `Syntax.lean` documents: `public` is
    27	//! `read <- allow`; an omitted rule is `deny`; an unnamed `update <- R` is
    28	//! `R[old] and R[next]` (OPEN R2); positional keys become named equalities
    29	//! on `id` (an `id`-typed or `t`-typed single key) or on the one declared
    30	//! unique key whose column types accept the arguments in order; in a
    31	//! `where`, each `.col = e` conjunct (e not reading the row) is a pin and the
    32	//! remaining conjuncts are the filter; `return insert …` is a bound write
    33	//! followed by `return`.
    34	//!
    35	//! **Erased, with the reason.** `sync …` and `online only` (residency
    36	//! decides what a device holds, never a server outcome) and non-unique
    37	//! `by` indexes (tuning; reads choose indexes themselves). A `text <= N`
    38	//! bound is not modelled as a value restriction (OPEN W6):
    39	//! [`LeanModule::store`] and [`LeanModule::tag_args`] refuse inputs that exceed
    40	//! it, and a literal written past it is unsupported. The surface emitter does
    41	//! use the bound to keep PAGE cases with nonportable synthesized keys out of
    42	//! the fragment before the oracle. A computed text written to a bounded column
    43	//! is not checked.
    44	//!
    45	//! **Everything else** outside the model's core fragment is an
    46	//! [`Unsupported`] with a stable `reason` (counted by the harness, never a
    47	//! pass) and a `detail` naming the construct. A translation is all or
    48	//! nothing: there is no partial program.

   108	        Ok(match t {
   109	            TypeKind::Int | TypeKind::Time => Kind::Int,

   111	            TypeKind::IntRange { .. } => return no("int-range", "an int range"),
   112	            TypeKind::Text { min: None, max, format: None } => Kind::Text(Some(*max)),
   113	            TypeKind::Text { format: Some(_), .. } => return no("text-format", "a text format"),
   114	            TypeKind::Text { min: Some(_), .. } => return no("text-minimum", "a text minimum length"),
   115	            TypeKind::Id => Kind::Id(IdSort::Plain),
   116	            TypeKind::Principal => Kind::Id(IdSort::Principal),
   117	            TypeKind::Ref { table } => Kind::Id(IdSort::Ref(table.clone())),
   118	            TypeKind::Bool => Kind::Bool,
   119	            TypeKind::Cursor => Kind::Cursor,
   120	            TypeKind::Decimal { .. } => return no("type-decimal", "decimal"),
   121	            TypeKind::Money { .. } => return no("type-money", "money"),
   122	            TypeKind::Json { .. } => return no("type-json", "json"),
   123	            TypeKind::Bytes { .. } => return no("type-bytes", "bytes"),
   124	            TypeKind::Image { .. } | TypeKind::Video { .. } | TypeKind::File { .. } => return no("type-asset", "an asset type"),

   134	/// A static type, as far as the fragment needs one.
   135	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]

   138	    Row(String),
   139	    Unknown,

   142	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
   143	struct Col {

   146	    nullable: bool,

   153	struct Table {

   172	/// A checked program set, translated.
   173	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
   174	pub struct LeanModule {
   175	    tables: Vec<Table>,
   176	    /// Surface declarations retained only for fragment eligibility. The model
   177	    /// omits physical indexes, so PAGE must reject cases whose synthesized
   178	    /// source or target key cannot fit every store before asking the oracle.
   179	    surface_tables: Vec<ast::TableDecl>,
   180	    /// `{"tables":[…]}` of `Syntax.lean`'s `Schema`.
   181	    pub schema: Json,
   182	    /// `Helper`s.
   183	    pub helpers: Json,
   184	    /// Each program, or why it is outside the fragment.
   185	    pub programs: BTreeMap<String, R<Json>>,
   186	    args: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(String, Kind, bool)>>,
   187	}
   188	
   189	/// Why [`lean`] produced no module.
   190	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   191	pub enum LeanError {
   192	    /// The sources do not compile; the model takes only checked programs.
   193	    Diagnostics(Vec<String>),
   194	    /// A schema-level construct outside the fragment.
   195	    Unsupported(Unsupported),
   196	}
   197	
   198	/// Check `sources` with [`crate::compile`], then translate their surface
   199	/// trees. A program outside the fragment is recorded per program in
   200	/// [`LeanModule::programs`]; a schema construct outside it refuses the whole
   201	/// module.
   202	pub fn lean(sources: &[(String, String)]) -> Result<LeanModule, LeanError> {
   203	    let bound = crate::compile(sources);
   204	    if !bound.diagnostics.is_empty() {
   205	        return Err(LeanError::Diagnostics(bound.diagnostics.iter().map(|d| format!("{}: {}", d.code, d.message)).collect()));
   206	    }
   207	    let documents: Vec<Document> = sources.iter().map(|(file, source)| crate::parse_document(file, source).0).collect();
   208	    let expiry_orders = bound.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
   209	        let column = table.expire.as_deref()?;
   210	        table.indexes.iter().find(|(_, index)| index.is_plain()
   211	            && index.columns().first().map(String::as_str) == Some(column))
   212	            .map(|(_, index)| (name.clone(), index.columns()))
   213	    }).collect();
   214	    from_documents_with_expiry(&documents, &expiry_orders).map_err(LeanError::Unsupported)
   215	}
   216	
   217	/// Translate documents that [`crate::compile`] has accepted. Callers that
   218	/// have not checked them must use [`lean`].
   219	pub fn from_documents(documents: &[Document]) -> R<LeanModule> {
   220	    from_documents_with_expiry(documents, &BTreeMap::new())
   221	}
   222	
   223	fn from_documents_with_expiry(documents: &[Document], expiry_orders: &BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>) -> R<LeanModule> {
   224	    for d in documents {
   225	        for (present, what) in [
   226	            (!d.maintains.is_empty(), "maintain"),
   227	            (!d.timelines.is_empty(), "timeline"),
   228	            (!d.views.is_empty() || !d.feed_views.is_empty(), "view"),
   229	            (!d.effects.is_empty(), "effect"),
   230	            (!d.shapes.is_empty(), "shape"),
   231	            (!d.actions.is_empty(), "action"),
   232	            (!d.routes.is_empty(), "route"),
   233	            (!d.schedules.is_empty(), "schedule"),
   234	            (d.identity.is_some(), "identity"),
   235	        ] {
   236	            if present {
   237	                return no(&format!("declaration-{what}"), format!("a {what} declaration in {}", d.file));
   238	            }
   239	        }
   240	    }
   241	    let decls: Vec<&ast::TableDecl> = documents.iter().flat_map(|d| d.tables.iter()).collect();
   242	    let mut tables = Vec::new();
   243	    for t in &decls {
   244	        tables.push(table_shape(t)?);
   245	    }
   246	    let module_tables = tables.clone();
   247	    let mut schema_tables = Vec::new();
   248	    for (t, shape) in decls.iter().zip(&tables) {
   249	        schema_tables.push(table_json(t, shape, &module_tables, expiry_orders.get(&t.name))?);
   250	    }
   251	    let functions: Vec<&ast::FunctionDecl> = documents.iter().flat_map(|d| d.functions.iter()).collect();
   252	    let helper_names: Vec<String> = functions.iter().map(|f| f.name.clone()).collect();
   253	    let mut module = LeanModule {
   254	        tables,
   255	        surface_tables: decls.iter().map(|table| (*table).clone()).collect(),
   256	        schema: json!({"tables": schema_tables}),
   257	        helpers: json!([]),
   258	        programs: BTreeMap::new(),
   259	        args: BTreeMap::new(),
   260	    };
   261	    let mut helpers = Vec::new();
   262	    for f in &functions {
   263	        let ast::FunctionBody::Expression(body) = &f.body else {
   264	            return no("helper-block", format!("helper {} has a block body", f.name));
   265	        };
   266	        let mut scope = Scope::new(&module, &helper_names);
   267	        for a in &f.args {
   268	            if a.type_.optional {
   269	                return no("helper-optional-parameter", format!("{}({})", f.name, a.name));
   270	            }
   271	            scope.vars.insert(a.name.clone(), Ty::Scalar(Kind::of(&a.type_.kind)?));
   272	        }
   273	        let body = scope.expr(body)?;
   274	        helpers.push(json!({"name": f.name, "params": f.args.iter().map(|a| a.name.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), "body": body}));
   275	    }
   276	    module.helpers = Json::Array(helpers);
   277	    let programs: Vec<&ast::ProgramDecl> = documents.iter().flat_map(|d| d.programs.iter()).collect();
   278	    let mut signatures = BTreeMap::new();
   279	    for p in &programs {
   280	        let args = p.args.iter().map(|a| Ok((a.name.clone(), Kind::of(&a.type_.kind)?, a.type_.optional))).collect::<R<Vec<_>>>();
   281	        if let Ok(args) = &args {
   282	            module.args.insert(p.name.clone(), args.clone());
   283	        }
   284	        signatures.insert(p.name.clone(), args);
   285	    }
   286	    for p in &programs {
   287	        let result = signatures[&p.name].clone().and_then(|args| program(&module, &helper_names, p, &args));
   288	        module.programs.insert(p.name.clone(), result);
   289	    }
   290	    Ok(module)
   291	}

   293	fn table_shape(t: &ast::TableDecl) -> R<Table> {
   294	    for (present, what) in [
   295	        (t.receipts.is_some(), "receipts"),
   296	        (t.ephemeral.is_some(), "ephemeral"),
   297	        (!t.search.is_empty(), "search"),
   298	        (!t.immutable.is_empty(), "immutable"),
   299	        (!t.final_exists.is_empty(), "after-insert"),
   300	        (t.retain.is_some(), "retain"),
   301	    ] {
   302	        if present {
   303	            return no(&format!("table-{what}"), format!("table {} declares {what}", t.name));
   304	        }
   305	    }
   306	    let mut cols = Vec::new();
   307	    for c in &t.columns {
   308	        for (present, what) in [
   309	            (c.sequence.is_some(), "sequence"),
   310	            (c.written_by.is_some(), "written-by"),
   311	            (c.readable_by_audience, "audience-field"),
   312	            (c.maintained.is_some(), "maintained"),
   313	            (c.default.is_some(), "default"),
   314	        ] {
   315	            if present {
   316	                return no(&format!("column-{what}"), format!("{}.{}", t.name, c.name));
   317	            }
   318	        }
   319	        let kind = Kind::of(&c.type_.kind)?;
   320	        if kind == Kind::Cursor {
   321	            return no("type-cursor-column", format!("{}.{}", t.name, c.name));
   322	        }
   323	        // @ref LLP 3000.039#2 — an undeclared reference restricts; keep is the legacy meaning, spelled by absence.
   324	        let on_delete = match (&c.type_.kind, c.on_delete.as_ref().map(|(a, _)| *a)) {
   325	            (TypeKind::Ref { .. }, None | Some(OnDelete::Restrict)) => Some("restrict"),
   326	            (TypeKind::Ref { .. }, Some(OnDelete::Cascade)) => Some("cascade"),
   327	            (TypeKind::Ref { .. }, Some(OnDelete::SetNull)) => Some("setNull"),
   328	            _ => None,
   329	        };
   330	        cols.push(Col { name: c.name.clone(), kind, nullable: c.type_.optional, on_delete });
   331	    }
   332	    let mut uniques = Vec::new();
   333	    let mut codes = Vec::new();
   334	    for i in &t.indexes {
   335	        if !i.is_plain() {
   336	            return no("index-computed-or-words", format!("{} index {}", t.name, i.name));
   337	        }
   338	        if i.unique {
   339	            uniques.push(i.columns.clone());
   340	            codes.push(i.refusal.as_ref().map(|(code, _)| code.clone()));

diff --git a/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Maintained.lean b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Maintained.lean
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..241876980a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/lean/Quarry/Maintained.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+import Quarry.Store
+
+/-!
+# Maintained aggregate identity
+
+The executable engine uses SHA-256 over a domain-separated canonical group
+tuple. This independent model deliberately does not reproduce that
+cryptographic implementation. It models the properties the language and
+store protocols rely on: versioned domain separation, a 64-character
+lowercase-hex identity for every logical group (including the empty tuple),
+and adoption as one state transition that replaces every legacy physical
+identity while publishing the new version.
+-/
+
+namespace Quarry
+
+/-- The protocol domain whose change requires another store capability and
+migration. -/
+def maintainedIdDomainV1 : List Nat := cps "snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1"
+
+/-- A small independent digest abstraction. Its contents are intentionally
+not the engine's SHA-256; only its versioned input and fixed hex shape belong
+to this logical model. -/
+def maintainedIdV1 (key : Key) : List Nat :=
+  (List.range 64).map fun i =>
+    let nibble := (maintainedIdDomainV1.length + (encKey key).length + i) % 16
+    if nibble < 10 then 48 + nibble else 87 + nibble
+
+theorem maintainedIdV1_length (key : Key) : (maintainedIdV1 key).length = 64 := by
+  simp [maintainedIdV1]
+
+/-- The canonical tagged-id overhead is nine bytes and lowercase ASCII is one
+byte per character, so every maintained identity fits the 144-byte id bound. -/
+theorem maintainedIdV1_fits (key : Key) : 9 + (maintainedIdV1 key).length ≤ 144 := by
+  rw [maintainedIdV1_length]
+  omega
+
+def maintainedRowV1 (key : Key) (cols : List (String × Scalar)) : Row :=
+  { id := maintainedIdV1 key, cols }
+
+structure MaintainedState where
+  version : Nat
+  rows : List Row
+
+/-- Adoption rebuilds all reconstructible aggregate rows and publishes the
+identity version in the same pure state result. `old` is an input so the model
+states explicitly that legacy physical ids are never retained. -/
+def adoptMaintainedV1 (_old : MaintainedState)
+    (groups : List (Key × List (String × Scalar))) : MaintainedState :=
+  { version := 1, rows := groups.map fun group => maintainedRowV1 group.1 group.2 }
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_version (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).version = 1 := rfl
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_ids (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.id = groups.map fun group => maintainedIdV1 group.1 := by
+  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
+
+theorem adoptMaintainedV1_values (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
+    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.cols = groups.map Prod.snd := by
+  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
+
+example : (maintainedIdV1 []).length = 64 := maintainedIdV1_length []
+example : (maintainedIdV1 [.id (List.replicate 64 97), .text (List.replicate 64 120)]).length = 64 :=
+  maintainedIdV1_length _
+
+end Quarry

+/-- Whether a row remains before its table's upper read lifetime. Null has no

+-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#3-semantics — upper read lifetimes filter every logical read before physical cleanup.
+def unexpired (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
+  match td.expire with
+  | none => true

+    | .null => true
+    | .int closes => now < closes

+/-- Referential actions ignore expired child images but still govern a child

+/-- Apply actions to the physical store using only the rows that are logically
+live as action witnesses. The root may itself be absent from `witnesses`. -/
+def refDeleteFrom (sch : Schema) (witnesses physical : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Except Stop Store :=
+  let cl := closure sch witnesses (storeSize sch witnesses + 1) [(t, old)] [(t, old)]
+  if restricted sch witnesses cl then throw (.refuse "E_REFERENCED")
+  else
+    let physical := cl.foldl (fun s (parent, row) => (referencing sch parent).foldl (fun s (child, col, action) =>
+      if action == .setNull then
+        ((witnesses child).filter fun k => names k col row.id && !inClosure cl child k).foldl
+          (fun s k => s.replaceRow child k (clearCol k col)) s
+      else s) s) physical
+    pure (cl.foldl (fun s p => s.removeRow p.1 p.2) physical)
+
+/-! ## Expiry retirement (LLP 3000.036.003 §6; LLP 3000.039 §3) -/
+
+def expired (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
+  match td.expire with
+  | none => false
+  | some c => match r.get c with
+    | .int closes => closes <= now
+    | _ => false
+
+def stored (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
+  (s t).any fun current => current.id == r.id
+
+/-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never
+stops later due keys; cascade and set-null are committed with the root. The
+model has no read-through retained-history rows, so every non-restricted due
+root can be retired immediately. -/
+def sweepExpired (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store :=
+  sch.tables.foldl (fun s td => (s td.name).foldl (fun s r =>
+    if expired td now r && stored s td.name r then
+      match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s td.name r with
+      | .ok next => next
+      | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => s
+      | .error _ => s
+    else s) s) s
+

   | .insert t fields ifAbsent =>

+/-- An eager snapshot of the declared table rows used while sweeping. A
+`Store` update is a functional closure over the previous store; repeatedly
+retiring rows through that representation retains an exponentially growing
+evaluation tree. Snapshotting after each successful retirement changes only
+the representation, while preserving table order and action sequencing. -/
+abbrev MaterialStore := Array (String × List Row)
+
+def materialRows (tables : List String) (s : Store) : MaterialStore :=
+  tables.toArray.map fun t => (t, s t)
+
+def MaterialStore.store (rows : MaterialStore) (fallback : Store) : Store := fun t =>
+  match rows.find? fun p => p.1 == t with
+  | some (_, rs) => rs
+  | none => fallback t
+
+-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — sweep each due root transactionally in table order.
 /-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never
 stops later due keys; cascade and set-null are committed with the root. The
 model has no read-through retained-history rows, so every non-restricted due
 root can be retired immediately. -/
 def sweepExpired (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store :=

-      | .ok next => next
-      | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => s
-      | .error _ => s
-    else s) s) s
+  let tables := sch.tables.map (·.name)
+  let rows := sch.tables.foldl (fun rows td =>
+    let physical := rows.store s
+    (physical td.name).foldl (fun rows r =>
+      let physical := rows.store s
+      if expired td now r && stored physical td.name r then
+        match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch physical now) physical td.name r with
+        | .ok next => materialRows tables next
+        | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => rows
+        | .error _ => rows
+      else rows) rows) (materialRows tables s)
+  rows.store s

+    let mut e = groups();

+    let target = schema.tables["totals"].clone();

+    let tx = e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();

+        tx.delete("totals", &target, &old).unwrap();
+        let mut legacy = old.clone();

+        if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut legacy {
+            fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(id));

+        "DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key=?1",
+        [crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_META],

+    e.adopt_at(next.schema, next.programs, 10).unwrap();
+    let rows = e.store().rows("totals").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(rows.len(), 1);

## 7. Formal and generated semantics

The Lean table schema carries optional lower and upper lifetime fields. Its
`live` projection filters every logical row lookup, scan, probe and write result
at the case clock. Physical write-target lookup can still resolve an unopened,
unexpired row, but an expired target is `NOT_FOUND`; an ordinary insert or
upsert evaluates insert authority against the pre-retirement logical store,
retires an expired same-id predecessor with its referential actions, then checks
the new image's remaining unique keys against live occupants. `insert if absent`
preflights all of those live unique-key collisions before same-id retirement; a
collision is a no-op and preserves the expired predecessor and its children.
The emitter includes both lifetime fields and independently selects the first
eligible plain expiry index from the checked physical index catalog. This
qualifies sweep execution for the selected physical plan; it does not
independently re-prove the compiler's index synthesis. The model's explicit physical sweep
uses the same cascade/restrict/set-null closure as delete, retains a restricted
root and continues to later due rows. It eagerly rematerializes the declared
table snapshot after each retirement; this is extensionally the same sequential
store update while avoiding an exponential functional-update expression tree.
The formal sweep carries the same in-engine, across-call continuation as the server: the
last visited table rotates the next call even after a complete scan, and a
call stopped at its visited-row bound retains each table's last
`(selected index components,id)` key until the following call scans its tail
and wrapped head.
The Lean difftest generator preserves
seeded expiry values and requested prelude/final sweeps, advances the formal
store with each engine sweep, then compares the following program outcome.

The difftest AST and generator produce null/past/future/equal-boundary openings,
opening plus expiry, membership witnesses and caps. Its first formal fragment
has no prelude or separately seeded clock: rows are seeded and evaluated under
one operation clock with openings at null, clock-minus-one, clock, and
clock-plus-one. That fragment proves the pure `live(now)` projection without
claiming to model the durable pending ledger or its bounded publication loop.
Native runtime, simulator and both device-store lifecycle suites cover
lower/upper composition, publication, rescheduling, restart, hostile device
clocks and server-floor rollback.

## 8. Compiled recipe

The `time` and `recipes` cards carry one executable timed-disclosure recipe. It
states separately:

Every step is inside the mutation's transaction: a refusal anywhere (a
`restrict`, a read-through child, the meter) aborts the whole mutation, and

An ordinary authored delete derives its closure and action witnesses from the
logical unexpired store, then applies the resulting actions to the physical
store. An expired child therefore neither blocks a `restrict` nor receives a
`cascade` or `set null` action merely because cleanup has not removed its
image yet.

**Expiry is a referential-action trigger.** A parent whose `expire at` passes
is logically absent at that instant, independent of whether physical cleanup
can retire it. Every path that physically retires an expired image — scheduled
sweep, an already-expired birth at commit, and same-id replacement of an
expired predecessor — applies steps 3–6 above in the same transaction. It
bypasses only the expired root's authored read/delete authorization; it does
not bypass `cascade`, `set null`, `restrict`, read-through retention,
constraints, maintains or partition events on affected rows.

For an insert or upsert that reuses an expired predecessor's id, insert
authority is evaluated against the pre-retirement logical store. The engine
then retires the predecessor through the action path before the remaining
uniqueness checks and physical insertion. At mutation commit, every row born
or updated into an expired final image is retired through that same path. A
refusal in any of these retirements aborts the whole mutation, including
earlier cascade and set-null writes. An unreadable expired predecessor does not
veto actionable retirement. If the table declares a read-through child, a
writer who cannot read the predecessor receives the insert's ordinary rule
refusal before the engine probes physical child occupancy; that occupancy
cannot disclose a hidden expired identity as a unique constraint.

This commit-end rule also covers a source of a row-keyed maintained view. The
source's final image first reaches normal maintenance, then its expired image
is retired through the common action path in the same transaction. No derived
maintenance shortcut may physically remove that source before closure
preflight: doing so would bypass a live `restrict` child and could orphan a
`cascade` or `set null` child. The source contribution and its retirement
cancel within the transaction, so an already-expired birth never enters a
committed count basis. The execution retains at most one retirement key per
changed source row; its allocation is charged when first retained and the
program's existing rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.

Seed commits preserve ordinary expired fixture images for the later sweep,
but sources of row-keyed views keep the established count-basis exception.
After normal maintenance, the seed filters its commit-end expiry tracker to
those sources and retires them through this same common action path. The
retirement uses the engine-owned, unbounded meter after the authored seed
work has been charged; applies `restrict`, `cascade`, and `set null`; and
defers the resulting maintained deltas until the retirement pass completes.
This prevents a born-expired source from reviving under a later clock
rollback without broadening retirement to unrelated fixture or raw-load
rows. The SQLite and evaluation Postgres seed adapters share this ordering;
the wasm interpreter has no server seed API or physical expiry-retirement
path.

A live `restrict` child, or a physically retained read-through child outside
the cascade closure but below a row in it, keeps the expired root physically
stored and the sweep continues to later due keys. A read-through child inside
the closure is removed first and is not a blocker. The action walk preflights
both kinds of blocker before its first set-null or cascade write. The retained
root remains logically unreadable.
Short sweeps preserve both a per-table row continuation and a rotating table
continuation. Repeated bounded calls therefore cannot restart forever at the
same restricted or read-through-retained roots, and a blocked earlier table
cannot starve due rows in a later table. After reaching a table's end its row
cursor wraps for roots whose blockers were removed.
Expired children are not live restrict witnesses, as in step 4. A read-through
child remains the stricter physical exception because its stored image depends
on its parent. Other errors after an earlier cascade or set-null write roll
back the whole retirement transaction. A restrict or physical read-through
blocker is expected deferred cleanup, not an error for the sweep as a whole.

update's constraint check asks whether the writer can read the row; an

//! Born-expired writes release server capacity without manufacturing device
//! occupancy. Both adapters keep deferral through settlement and reopening.
use super::*;
use snapback4_core::{Engine, WriteState};
use serde_json::json;

fn counts<S: DeviceStore>(device: &mut Device<S>, all: u64, a: u64, b: u64) {
    let tx = device.store.transaction().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(tx.cap_count("items", &[], &[]).unwrap(), all);
    for (group, n) in [("a", a), ("b", b), ("c", 0)] {
        assert_eq!(tx.cap_count("items", &["group".into()], &[Value::String(group.into())]).unwrap(), n);
    }
    assert!(tx.get("items", "born").unwrap().is_none());
    tx.rollback().unwrap();
}

fn retired_birth<S: DeviceStore>(store: S) {
    let source = include_str!("../../../snapback4-core/tests/fixtures/expired-birth-cap.q");
    let b = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
    assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    let mut server = Engine::memory(b.schema.clone(), b.programs.iter().map(|p| p.program.clone())).unwrap();
    let backend = Backend { generation: server.generation(), schema: b.schema, programs: b.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program).collect() };
    let mut device = Device::open_store(store, Some(backend)).unwrap();
    let snapshot = server.snapshot_acquisition_page_at("alice", None, 100, 100).unwrap();
    let page = decoded(&json!({"snapshot":true, "watermark":snapshot.watermark, "more":false,
        "generation":server.generation(), "held":snapshot.held, "acquisitions":snapshot.acquisitions, "events":[]}).to_string()).unwrap();
    device.apply(&page, true).unwrap();
    let mut previous = (0, 0, 0);
    for (id, group, until, all, a, b, succeeds) in [
        ("born", "a", Value::Int(0), 0, 0, 0, true),
        ("live", "a", Value::Null, 1, 1, 0, true),
        ("group-full", "a", Value::Null, 1, 1, 0, false),
        ("other", "b", Value::Null, 2, 1, 1, true),
        ("table-full", "c", Value::Null, 2, 1, 1, false),
    ] {
        let args = json!({"id":id, "group":group, "until":wire::to_json(&until)});
        let entry: Queued = decoded(&json!({"id":id,"seq":0,"op":"add","args":args,
            "viewer":"alice","now":100,"predictable":true}).to_string()).unwrap();
        let admitted = device.admit(entry).unwrap();
        assert!(!admitted.predictable && admitted.predicted.is_empty(), "{admitted:?}");
        counts(&mut device, previous.0, previous.1, previous.2);
        device = Device::open_store(device.store, None).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(device.queued().unwrap(), [admitted]);
        let out = server.mutate("add", Some(id), Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
            ("id".into(), Value::Id(id.into())), ("group".into(), Value::String(group.into())), ("until".into(), until),
        ])).at(100)).unwrap();
        let seq = if succeeds {
            let WriteState::Sent { seq, .. } = out.state else { panic!("{out:?}") };
            Some(seq)
        } else {
            assert!(matches!(out.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_CONSTRAINT"), "{out:?}");
            None
        };
        let tx = server.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(tx.cap_count("items", &[], &[]).unwrap(), all);
        assert!(tx.get("items", "born").unwrap().is_none());
        tx.rollback().unwrap();
        device.settle(id, seq).unwrap();
        let from = device.state().unwrap().0;
        let page = server.stream_at("alice", from, 100, 100).unwrap();
        assert!(page.events.iter().all(|e| e.id != "born"), "retirement withdraws all born-row events");
        let page: StreamPage = decoded(&json!({"snapshot":false,"requested_watermark":from,
            "images_at":page.images_at,"joined":page.joined,"acquisitions":page.acquisitions,
            "watermark":page.watermark,"more":page.more,"generation":server.generation(),
            "events":page.events.iter().map(|e| json!({"table":e.table,"kind":e.kind,"id":e.id,
                "data":e.data.as_ref().map(wire::to_json)})).collect::<Vec<_>>()}).to_string()).unwrap();
        device.apply(&page, false).unwrap();
        counts(&mut device, all, a, b);
        device = Device::open_store(device.store, None).unwrap();
        counts(&mut device, all, a, b);
        assert!(device.queued().unwrap().is_empty());
        previous = (all, a, b);
    }
    assert_eq!(server.sweep_expired(100, 2_000).unwrap(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn retired_birth_keeps_memory_device_caps_exact() {
    retired_birth(crate::memory::MemoryStore::new());
}

#[test]
fn retired_birth_keeps_sqlite_device_caps_exact() {
    publication_tests::with_sqlite(retired_birth);
}

     7	/// Typechecked, terminating work which cannot read, write, mint or refuse.

     9	pub fn total_expr(expr: &Expr) -> bool {

    11	        Expr::Literal(_) | Expr::Variable(_) | Expr::Input(Input::Viewer | Input::Now | Input::ReadTime) => true,
    12	        Expr::Input(Input::NewId) | Expr::Get(_) | Expr::Exists(_) | Expr::Scan(_) | Expr::Merge(_) => false,
    13	        Expr::Field { base, .. } | Expr::Unary { op: UnaryOp::Not, value: base } => total_expr(base),
    14	        Expr::Unary { op: UnaryOp::Neg, .. } => false,
    15	        Expr::Array(values) => values.iter().all(total_expr),
    16	        Expr::Object(fields) => fields.values().all(total_expr),
    17	        Expr::Shape { base, fields } => total_expr(base) && fields.values().all(total_expr),

   102	pub fn predict(rows: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, program: &Program, mut context: Context, ceilings: Ceilings) -> Result<Prediction, RuntimeError> {

   120	    }

   122	    // whole mutation; no actual transition hook would run for that case.

   124	        return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("timeline follow/unfollow/refollow requires online-only slot accounting".into()));
   125	    }

   127	    runner.device = true;
   128	    runner.device_allowance = Some(Meter::new(ceilings, Cut::Abort));
   129	    let result = runner.run(program).and_then(|value| {

   149	    // the server's (it can refuse that insert first): the write queues and the server's verdict stands.

   192	pub fn native_observation(rows: &dyn Rows, schema: &Schema, module: &super::native::Module, program: &Program, mut context: Context, ceilings: Ceilings) -> (Result<QueryOutcome, Refusal>, bool, bool, super::components::Provenance) {

   241	    pub(super) fn device_work<T>(&mut self, work: impl FnOnce(&mut Self) -> Result<T, RuntimeError>) -> Result<T, RuntimeError> {
   242	        let Some(allowance) = self.device_allowance.take() else { return work(self) };
   243	        let (caller, entered) = self.enter_device_work(allowance);
   244	        let result = entered.and_then(|_| work(self));
   245	        self.leave_device_work(caller, result.as_ref().err())?;
   246	        result
   247	    }

            if kind == "upsert" { rule_sites(schema, &definition.rules.insert, &format!("upsert {table} insert rule"), &mut fact.sites, &mut BTreeSet::new()); }
            // Final-exists constraints retain declaration order; target and
            // index are not identities when several declarations probe them.
            for (ordinal, (target, index, key)) in definition.constraints.iter().filter_map(|constraint| match constraint {
                snapback4_core::schema::Constraint::FinalExistsOnInsert { table, index, key } => Some((table, index, key)),
                _ => None,
            }).enumerate() {
                let location = format!("after insert {table} constraint {ordinal}");
                fact.sites.push(site(schema, &location, target, index, "rule"));
                for term in key { rule_term_sites(schema, term, &location, &mut fact.sites, &mut BTreeSet::new(), true); }
                aggregate_source_site(schema, target, &location, &mut fact.sites);
            }
        }
    }
    let server = fact.sites.iter().any(|site| site.class == SiteClass::Server);
    match program.kind {
        ProgramKind::Query => fact.runs = Some(if server { "server" } else { "device" }.into()),
        ProgramKind::Mutation => fact.predicts = Some(if server { "never" } else { "eligible" }.into()),
        ProgramKind::Job => fact.runs = Some("server".into()),
        ProgramKind::Action => { fact.runs = Some("server".into()); fact.predicts = Some("never".into()); }
    }
    fact.components = components::plan(program);
    fact
}

fn field_only_updates(body: &[Stmt], table: &str, definition: &snapback4_core::schema::Table) -> bool {
    let owned = |patch: &Expr| matches!(patch, Expr::Object(fields) if !fields.is_empty() && fields.keys().all(|field| definition.written_by.contains_key(field)));
    body.iter().all(|stmt| match stmt {
        Stmt::Update { table: target, patch, .. } if target == table => owned(patch),
        Stmt::WriteTarget { target, patch, upsert: false, .. } if target.table == table => owned(patch),
        Stmt::If { then_body, else_body, .. } => field_only_updates(then_body, table, definition) && field_only_updates(else_body, table, definition),
        Stmt::For { body, .. } => field_only_updates(body, table, definition),
        _ => true,
    })
}

    pub fn write_reservation(&self, source: &str) -> Option<WriteReservation> {

            if plan.birth.is_none() && !table.maintained.is_empty() { return None; }

                source == f.messages || source == f.members || source == f.runs
                || (source == f.scope && matches!(kind, "insert" | "upsert"))) {

- **Device prediction omits commit-end expiry actions.** [device.rs:1056](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-device/src/device.rs:1056) commits `local::predict` without consuming the expiry tracker populated at [write.rs:978](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-w12-lang/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/write.rs:978). With fully acquired public tables, an authorized update changing a live parent’s expiry to `0` remains predictable. The device retains its cascade children and unchanged set-null references; the server’s commit-end retirement deletes or clears them. A restrict child instead makes the server refuse while the device predicts success. The same-id guard does not cover updates. Execute retirement before device final obligations, or queue these mutations without predicted rows.
